info.title: Aius device control API
info.description: Bounded HTTP control and telemetry surface served by the Aius Teensy optical processor. The app hosts this document; the device serves the described routes.

deviceHost.description: Teensy Ethernet host and optional port

get.description: Compact status for the editor's flow ends (Phase 4f F3): exactly carrier, state, sample_rate, pipeline_diag.codec_pc, tx_gate.open and tx_gate.replay_running, under the full body's names and nesting and from the same sources. Under 512 bytes. GET only; POST answers 405.
Read-only single effective DSP configuration: source, features, input channels, output EQ, downmix matrix, and limiter. It performs no SD or flash I/O.

put.description: Authenticated, validated, bounded replacement of the effective DSP configuration. The body carries the same eight keys the GET returns plus base_generation; all nine are required, source must be the literal "sd", and unknown or duplicate keys are rejected. A 200 means the write to /aius/dsp.json is durable and the validated model is staged, not that it is live: the apply and the config_generation increment happen at the next audio block boundary. An invalid body, a stale base_generation, or an SD failure leave both SD and the active DSP snapshot untouched.

200.description: Body validated and written to /aius/dsp.json. Emitted once the SD job completes; the model is staged, and the apply plus config_generation increment happen at the next audio block boundary.

400.description: The body failed the bounded parser: malformed JSON, an empty body, a missing, unknown, or duplicate key, a wrong type, an out-of-range value, more than two EQ sections, a source other than "sd", an unsupported EQ type, or a body over 12,288 bytes. The specific parser error code is not returned; every rejection collapses to dsp_config_invalid. Neither SD nor the active DSP snapshot is touched.

401.description: The X-Aius-SD-Auth header is absent or does not match the token printed by the physical USB command AIUS AUTH.

409.description: base_generation does not equal the device's current config_generation. Re-read GET /api/dsp/config and retry against the generation it reports. Neither SD nor the active DSP snapshot is touched.

413.description: Rejected by the HTTP transport before the handler runs: request line, headers, and body together filled the 13,312-byte request buffer (request_too_large), or Content-Length overflowed a uint32 or was smaller than the body bytes already received (body_too_large). A body between 12,289 bytes and the buffer limit instead reaches the parser and returns 400.

500.description: Emitted asynchronously by the SD job: the validated body could not be committed because a rename of the temporary or backup file failed. The previous /aius/dsp.json is restored and the staged model is discarded.

503.description: The SD card is not ready (sd_unavailable), or another SD job is already in flight (sd_busy). audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the body parse's or the store job's start cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry. Neither SD nor the active DSP snapshot is touched.

507.description: Emitted asynchronously by the SD job: the body could not be written to the card. The temporary file is removed and the previous configuration is left in place.

get.description: Read-only coherent snapshot of the DSP pipeline: per-input and stereo-output levels, the limiter's gain reduction, a bounded waveform envelope, and the target adapter's own block telemetry. The audio path accumulates per block and publishes a complete snapshot behind a seqlock about 20 times a second; this route copies the last complete one and never blocks the audio callback. Every value is diagnostic and none of it is configuration. The response is fixed-size and performs no SD or flash I/O.

200.description: Coherent meter snapshot. A sequence of 0 is a valid 200 meaning nothing has been published yet - metering is bypassed by features.meters, or no audio block has been processed since the last config apply - and is rendered as "no data" rather than as a zero-level signal.

live.summary: Playing 5.1 material with the limiter working

never_published.summary: Metering bypassed, or no block processed yet - a valid 200, not an error

500.description: The snapshot could not be copied coherently: a publish straddled every one of the reader's eight bounded seqlock retries, so the device refused rather than return a torn mix of two windows. Retry. It never means the meters are unavailable - that state is a 200 with sequence 0.

get.description: Read-only view of the measurement loopback session: the capture state machine, the analysis figures once published, and the stimulus floors beside them. The capture is a software tap at the S/PDIF transmit producer - the words the DSP commits to the ring are the words on the wire - so stimulus and capture share one sample grid and the figures are immune to physical clock error by construction (the clock/content ratio surface stays with the physical loop). Reads memory only.

200.description: The session. `figures` is null until an analysis pass completes; `fail_reason` is "none" outside the failed state. The floors are properties of the 16-bit replay stimulus, not of the analysis: THD+N and SNR bottom out near -96 dB, Goertzel harmonic THD stays usable to about -95 dBc, and the -140 dB inter-stage claim is host-proven only - no 16-bit transport can verify it on-device. SNR's harmonic exclusion additionally inherits the harmonic estimate's leakage-limited accuracy (about -90 dB of the subtracted harmonic).

done.summary: A completed run against the 440 Hz baseline vector

idle.summary: No session has ever started - a valid 200, not an error

post.description: Arms a capture against a replay vector. Mutating, so it joins the control-route gate: the request needs the X-Aius-SD-Auth token. The natural order is arm first, then POST /api/replays/start - an armed capture tolerates 10 s without audio blocks before the epoch side times it out (2 s once capturing, and a cancelled capture is reclaimed after 1 s more). The capture latches the config generation and the overrun counter at arm and retires to failed if either moves: a config splice or a dropped block inside the window is exactly the seam artifact the loop-coherent stimulus exists to avoid.

split.summary: Per-channel fit frequencies for the two-tone vector

multitone.summary: Frequency-response probes for the multitone vector

400.description: measure_body: the body is not the documented shape - missing or invalid id, a duplicate or unknown key, a non-integer frequency, more than 8 probes, or trailing bytes.

409.description: measure_start: refused - a capture is already live (armed through analysing), or the analysis rejected the parameters (a frequency at or above fs/2).

get.description: One page of at most 8 ring entries after `cursor`, oldest first. The ring holds 32; pass the response's `next` back as `cursor` and keep polling while a page comes back full.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The last sequence already seen; the page starts after it, or at the oldest retained entry when the ring has moved past it.

post.description: Acknowledges before reboot. The connection then closes and subsequent requests require a new boot session. A reboot DESTROYS a frozen flight-recorder capture: recorder state is internal RAM and the boot probe resets the PSRAM chips.

get.description: Staged firmware-upgrade document (docs/plans/aius-ota-upgrade.md slice 3). The open read: it mutates nothing and is the one OTA route that takes no token, so a page can render the disabled or TEST KEY state. On a build without the AIUS_OTA option, or one reporting itself unavailable, every OTA route answers 404 ota_absent. This slice reaches state 'armed'; activation_available stays false until the later device-gated slice ships the flash trigger.

404.description: ota_absent: OTA compiled out or unavailable.

503.description: ota_status: the application could not fill the document.

put.description: One self-contained container chunk, the APPEND_PART protocol the replay upload uses: Content-Range says where the bytes belong in the FILE (a 256-byte header at offset 0 then the payload from 256), the body carries them whole (at most AIUS_OTA_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 4096), and the answer states the next file offset, so a dropped connection costs one chunk. The first chunk must carry the whole 256-byte header.

200.description: Chunk accepted; body is {"ok":true,"next_offset":N} (a FILE offset).

400.description: ota_chunk / ota_header: request-shape refusal (no range, span mismatch, over the chunk cap, or a first chunk shorter than the container header). ota_malformed / ota_unsupported: the container itself failed validation.

409.description: ota_range carries next_offset (resume there, exactly as the replay upload teaches); ota_disarmed / ota_state / ota_digest / ota_signature otherwise.

503.description: sd_unavailable (no card), or sd_busy: a root SD job holds the volume this instant - the retryable token every SD route speaks. Mid-stream chunks legitimately collide with root jobs (measured ~1 in 400 chunks, 2026-08-04); retry the same offset. Before the defect-2 conviction this case mis-answered 507 ota_storage, which read as a hard storage failure.

507.description: ota_storage: the staging medium genuinely refused (staging path or scratch construction failed, or the storage verdict from the core).

post.description: Verified to armed: arms the staged image for activation (aius_ota_arm_image). Token-gated. Not the feature latch, which the firmware arms at composition.

409.description: ota_disarmed / ota_state: the image is not verified.

post.description: Staged to verified: the incremental payload digest is checked against the container header, then the Ed25519 signature over the authentication digest against the compiled-in key, then the authenticated payload's image vector table (+0x1000: header tag, entry pointer, IVT self pointer) against the flash window the image must have been linked for (the canonical window under the slot-agnostic chooser; the boot window on a plain build). A container that is byte-perfect and correctly signed but is not a bootable image for this window (the 2026-08-16 Intel-hex-as-payload shape) is refused here, before any flash is spent. Token-gated; the ~80 ms Ed25519 check is one audio epoch's stall, so stage during silence.

409.description: ota_disarmed / ota_state (not staged) / ota_digest / ota_signature / ota_ivt (authentic, but the payload's IVT is not an image linked for this device's flash window; the session is failed exactly as for ota_digest, and POST /api/ota/abort returns it to idle).

post.description: Any state except activation-requested back to idle, discarding the staged image. Token-gated.

Programs the armed staged image into boot flash and resets into it. Token-gated, AND gated on the runtime activation latch: while the latch is off (its boot default) this answers 409 ota_activation_disabled and nothing happens, because the operator must first prove the scratch-sector recovery check on the bench (POST /api/ota/self-test-flash) and flip the latch (POST /api/ota/enable-activation). When enabled and the image is ARMED, the 200 acknowledgement is the LAST thing the client sees: the device drains this response, then quiesces (audio stopped, ISR sources parked), programs the flash inside a dark window and issues SYSRESETREQ, coming back on the new image. The device-gated activation surface (enable-activation, self-test-flash) is deliberately not in this contract.

200.description: Acknowledged before the board goes dark; body {"ok":true,"activating":true}. The next observable state is the board rebooting into the new image.

409.description: ota_activation_disabled: the runtime latch is off (activation not enabled on this device). ota_state: the image is not ARMED.

get.description: Flight-recorder bank status: active_slot, slots_recycled, the uniform trigger config, and every slot's own capture header in one document. Token-gated like every recorder route (each slot's header reveals its trigger state). On a board with no PSRAM fitted, every slot's state is 'absent' and every other recorder route refuses cleanly.

post.description: Operator freeze: sets the freeze token; the audio ISR acknowledges at its next block (or the epoch reclaims when blocks have stopped). The capture becomes readable once the state reaches 'frozen' - poll GET /api/recorder. During an automatic trigger's post-roll the request is counted as a suppressed trigger and answers 200 (first trigger wins; the capture in flight satisfies the ask).

200.description: Freeze accepted (state 'freezing' is transitional: postroll then draining then frozen).

409.description: recorder_state: absent board, or already draining/frozen.

post.description: Thaws the ACTIVE slot in place (no round-robin advance to the next slot): discards its frozen capture, increments its freeze_generation and re-arms it as the active slot. Destructive - pull the data first. The bank auto-advances to the next slot on every automatic trigger, so this route is now the operator's explicit override rather than the routine re-arm path - useful when the automatic advance is deferred by an outstanding read lease on the next slot, or to keep recording into the same slot rather than the next one.

409.description: recorder_state: not frozen (nothing to thaw), or absent board.

put.description: Installs the RAM-only trigger configuration (defaults return at boot). Every key is required exactly once - the DSP PUT's anti-drift stance. Allowed while recording or frozen; a capture in flight (postroll/draining) keeps the config it latched. gr_threshold_db 0 disables the GR trigger whatever its mask flag says.

400.description: recorder_body: not the documented shape - a missing/duplicate/unknown key, a positive gr_threshold_db, an exponent-carrying number, or trailing bytes.

409.description: recorder_state: absent board, or a capture in flight.

get.description: One bounded chunk of the ACTIVE slot's frozen ring, served straight from PSRAM in PHYSICAL ring order (the header's oldest_frame says where the stream starts; the committed host script firmware/tools/aius-recorder-pull.py unwraps and reassembles a WAV). Addressing a slot other than the active one is not yet wired - aius-recorder-rolling-buffer.md Phase C's still-owed remainder. offset and length are BYTES; offset must be frame-aligned (a multiple of 8); length is capped at chunk_max_bytes (65536) and clamped to the valid extent. generation must equal that slot's freeze_generation, so a thaw/re-freeze (or an auto-advance) between chunks can never splice two captures into one file. Chunks are idempotent - retry after a timeout drop. Query parameters are fixed-order: offset, length, generation.

200.description: Raw interleaved-LR s32le frames (24-bit LSB-aligned), exact Content-Length.

400.description: recorder_read: misaligned offset, zero length, or offset beyond the valid extent.

409.description: recorder_state: not frozen, or a stale freeze_generation.

get.description: Bounded listing of /aius/replays on the card: at most AIUS_OPTICAL_APP_INDEX_SCAN_MAX raw reads per request, refused with 503 sd_busy while any SD job owns the volume, and honest when it stops early - either bound (scan cap or response buffer) reports truncated:true with the rows already written intact. Public route (no token). A board without a card answers 200 with the error body shape (pre-cutover behaviour: missing media is reported in-body, not as a failed request).

200.description: The listing, or the in-body sd_unavailable error shape.

503.description: sd_busy: an SD job (refill, upload, download, probe) owns the volume; retry. audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the route's admission cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

delete.description: Deletes one replay vector by id (both the complete .iec and a .part are candidates; the body parser is strict - duplicate or unknown keys refuse). Two card primitives, gated on the volume like the listing.

409.description: replay_active: the selected vector is playing; stop it first.

503.description: sd_busy: an SD job owns the volume; retry.

post.description: Selects a complete .iec vector and starts replay; GET /api/replays/status reports the progression prebuffering -> playing. Refused while a live carrier owns the audio path (its own 409 token, replay_carrier_present, which clears when the carrier goes away rather than when the request changes).

loop.description: Restart at EOF instead of stopping; default false.

400.description: replay_body: malformed body, or no card mounted.

409.description: replay_carrier_present (live input owns the path) or replay_start (already active / start refused).

post.description: Stops the running replay (idempotent). The clock hands back to the input; with no carrier the board returns to its boot-idle digital silence, counted in the transmit ring's underruns.

get.description: The replay service's own record - selection, progression, queue depth and fault counters. Public route. State transitions also surface as type-3 events on /api/events, so a replay that ends by itself is never an unexplained 'stopped'.

put.description: Validates and atomically stores the firmware-owned public feature flags. This exception does not require the SD asset token.

503.description: sd_unavailable with no card; sd_busy while an SD job holds the volume. audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the body parse's or the store job's start cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

post.description: Selects the SDIO transfer mode for the next card mount: DMA (true) or FIFO (false). Takes X-Aius-SD-Auth. Not persisted: every boot starts in FIFO, so a watchdog reset during a DMA run reverts silently; read sd_diag.sd_mode from GET /api/status to confirm. Refused with 503 sd_busy while a file is open.

200.description: Mode recorded; the next mount uses it.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Nested asset path below www/. Maximum decoded length 96 bytes and eight path components; ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, and hyphen are accepted. It never ends in a slash: a trailing slash names a directory and is served by getSdIndex.

503.description: sd_unavailable with no card; sd_busy while an SD job holds the volume. audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the SD job's start cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

put.description: Atomically replaces a file under www/. The body is streamed directly to SD (so it needs a Content-Length; a chunked body is refused) and is limited by the card and uint32 Content-Length, not firmware RAM. Content-Range is ignored on this route: unlike the replay upload there is no chunked resume, one request is the whole file. The 200 is emitted only after the temp-and-backup replace commits durably. Refusal order is fixed: the *config.json write guard outranks authentication, which outranks media state.

403.description: The resource's name ends in config.json, which only PUT /api/config/public may write. The guard is a bare suffix match, so any filename ending in "config" trips it.

503.description: No SD card is mounted (sd_unavailable). audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the SD job's start cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

507.description: sd_upload covers two synchronous refusals -- an SD job already holds the volume (retry when idle), or the path/scratch build was refused -- and must not be presented as "card full"; sd_capacity is the card actually filling during the streamed write. An asynchronous write failure surfaces as 507 sd_write with the five-field SdJobError shape instead.

500.description: The streamed write completed but the final commit (temp-to-target replace) failed; the SdJobError counters say how far it got.

delete.description: Deletes a file under www/. Same guard order as PUT: the *config.json guard, then authentication, then media state.

403.description: The resource's name ends in config.json; the public config is not deletable here.

404.description: sd_path for a path the route grammar refuses; sd_not_found when nothing exists there.

503.description: sd_unavailable with no card; sd_busy while an SD job holds the volume. audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the SD job's start cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

/sd/{directory}/.description: The same /sd/ resource tree, spelled with a trailing slash: a directory index, so files uploaded to the card are discoverable without knowing their names. Only GET is defined; PUT and DELETE on a trailing-slash path answer 405 sd_directory, because a directory is neither an upload target nor a delete target.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: Directory below www/, without the trailing slash the path template supplies. www/ itself is the subtree root; /sd/ alone is not a route, so the card root is not browsable.

get.description: Lists one directory as HTML a browser renders directly: one relative link per entry back into the same /sd/ namespace, a byte size per file, a "../" link below the subtree root, and a footer stating the counts. HTML rather than JSON because the listing's purpose is discovery by a browser, and a JSON listing would need a page that has to be discovered first. The listing is capped at 64 entries per request and is not paginated: past the cap it stops and the footer reports truncated: yes. Only entries the download route could serve are listed - a name is at most 32 bytes of ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen - and the rest are counted in the footer's hidden total rather than drawn as dead links. Enumeration is refused while an SD job holds the volume.

200.description: The directory listing. The footer's three counts are the observable statement of the bound: entries shown, entries hidden because their names are not servable, and whether the listing was truncated by the 64-entry cap or by the response buffer.

listing.summary: Two entries at the subtree root, complete
listing.value:
/sd/www/

  • index.html 4096
  • sub/ dir

2 shown, 0 hidden, truncated: no. Sizes in bytes; at most 64 entries per listing.

truncated.summary: A directory larger than one listing
truncated.value:
/sd/www/

  • a.bin 12

64 shown, 3 hidden, truncated: yes. Sizes in bytes; at most 64 entries per listing.

404.description: sd_path for a directory outside the www/ subtree or one the download route would also refuse; sd_not_found when nothing exists there; sd_not_directory when the path names a file.

500.description: The response buffer could not hold even the listing's framing. Its body is HTML, like the 200, not the JSON error shape.

503.description: sd_unavailable with no card mounted; sd_busy while an SD job holds the volume, which is refused rather than queued; sd_index when the card refused the enumeration; sd_index_unavailable when the running firmware has no directory-enumeration callback wired.

DspConfigUpdate.description: The complete DSP model to store. The parser is bounded and allocation-free: it reads the body from the fixed request buffer, so the body is capped at 12,288 bytes and a larger one is rejected rather than truncated.

edit.summary: Dialogue lift, output high-pass, clip-free headroom, limiter on, against generation 7

SdAuth.name: X-Aius-SD-Auth
SdAuth.description: 16 hexadecimal characters printed by the physical USB command AIUS AUTH.

AudioBusy.description: audio_busy: shed while live input owns the transmit ring and the route's admission cost exceeds the ring margin (Phase 4f admission); carries Retry-After: 1; retry.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; the firmware sends 1 on every 503.

source.description: Which config is active: the const factory default or the SD override.

config_generation.description: Monotonic generation, incremented when a new config is applied at a block boundary.

staged_generation.description: Counter advanced once per committed staging (an SD load when it publishes, a PUT when its SD write commits, which is the instant its 200 is released and config_pending turns true; a PUT whose write faults leaves it unchanged), which config_generation deliberately is not: a carrier-less board never reaches the block-boundary apply, so config_generation stays 0 and this is the only way to tell one committed PUT from the next. Response-only; the PUT rejects it as an unknown key.

config_pending.description: true when this document describes the STAGED model awaiting a block boundary rather than the applied one. Response-only; the PUT rejects it as an unknown key.

output_eq.description: Stereo post-mix output EQ, up to two bounded sections.

DspConfigUpdate.description: PUT /api/dsp/config request model: the eight model keys DspConfig requires plus base_generation (DspConfig's staged_generation and config_pending are runtime-reported and rejected here). All nine are required and a duplicate key is rejected. Every number must be finite and its literal shorter than 64 characters; a non-finite or over-long numeric literal is out of range. Objects nest at most eight deep. Firmware is laxer than this schema in one place: an EQ section may omit frequency_hz, q, and gain_db, each defaulting to 0, so an omission round-trips only for "type": "bypass" (a non-bypass section then fails the 10 Hz and 0.1 Q lower bounds); gain_db alone may be omitted for any type. Sending all four fields, as this schema requires, is always accepted.

source.description: Must be the literal "sd"; a PUT always writes the SD override. Any other value is rejected.

config_generation.description: Required non-negative integer, echoed from the last GET. Its value is not otherwise validated; base_generation carries the concurrency check.

sample_rate_hz.description: Audio sample rate in hertz; must be a positive integer.

output_eq.description: Stereo post-mix output EQ, up to two bounded sections; a third section is rejected.

base_generation.description: Optimistic-concurrency token: the config_generation the edit was based on. A value other than the device's current config_generation returns 409 and touches nothing.

DspFeatures.description: Per-stage bypass flags; true keeps the stage active.

DspInputChannels.description: The six fixed input channels in AIUS channel-mask order.

eq.description: Per-input EQ, up to two bounded sections.

frequency_hz.description: Filter frequency in hertz; bounded 10 to 24000 for non-bypass sections.

q.description: Filter quality factor; bounded 0.1 to 20 for non-bypass sections.

gain_db.description: Peaking gain in decibels; bounded -24 to 24; zero for non-peaking sections.

center_gain_linear.description: Shared linear centre (FC) gain folded into both stereo channels; values above the default boost dialogue.

surround_gain_linear.description: Shared linear surround gain applied as SL-to-L and SR-to-R; controls rear-channel blend without swapping sides.

lfe_gain_linear.description: Linear LFE gain folded into each stereo channel.

lfe_crossover_hz.description: Corner frequency in hertz of the LR4 low-pass through which LFE folds into both stereo channels. 0 is deliberately outside the range: "no LFE" is lfe_gain_linear = 0, and a zero corner would be a second encoding of that one state.

clipfree.description: Whether the clip-free headroom policy is selected.

layout_aware.description: Whether the downmix resolves per-layout routes; optional on a PUT and reads true when absent, matching the firmware parser's absent-reads-on default.

surround_delay_ms.description: Surround decorrelation: SL and SR are delayed by this many milliseconds (symmetric) before their fold gain, de-correlating the surrounds from the fronts so the downmix keeps envelopment instead of comb-filtering correlated content. 0 is the bit-exact undelayed fold. Optional on a PUT and reads 0 when absent - the pre-feature behaviour, like layout_aware's absent-reads-on rule.

Meters.description: One coherent window of the pipeline, published behind a seqlock so a reader never observes a torn mix of two windows. Levels are dBFS floored at -120, so every number in this document is finite: log10(0) is not valid JSON and silence is a meter's resting state, so the device converts once with a documented floor rather than every client reinventing the clamp.

sequence.description: Strictly increasing publish counter. 0 means never published - metering is bypassed, or no audio block has been processed since the last config apply - and clients render it as "no data" rather than as a zero-level signal.

sample_rate_hz.description: Sample rate the published window was accumulated at. 0 accompanies a sequence of 0, because a never-published snapshot carries no window.

input.description: Exactly six positional entries in AIUS channel-mask order: fl, fr, fc, lfe, sl, sr. Position is the identity; there is deliberately no per-entry channel key. A channel absent from the decoded layout reports the floor.

limiter_gain_reduction_db.description: Limiter gain reduction in decibels at the instant of the publish, already dB and passed through unconverted. 0 means no reduction; -1000 is the limiter's defensive fully-closed value. Sampled once per published window rather than per audio block, so it is an instantaneous value, not the window's peak.

waveform.description: Bounded per-bucket peak-magnitude envelope of the last accumulated block, as per-mille integers of full scale, drawn mirrored about the centre line. The array's own length is the count; there is no separate waveform_count. Empty when nothing has been published.

queue_frames.description: Frames buffered in the audio output ring at the publish instant.

estimated_latency_us.description: queue_frames expressed as microseconds at the current sample rate.

dsp_cycles_last.description: DWT cycle count for the most recently completed audio block - the DSP, the meter accumulate, the ring write and any publish - measured on the device at 600 MHz.

dsp_cycles_max.description: Peak dsp_cycles_last since boot or since POST /api/clear, which resets this watermark alongside the block and overrun counters.

MeterLevel.description: One metered channel. Both values are finite dBFS at or above the -120 floor; the practical ceiling is about +48 dBFS, which only a decoder emitting beyond 24-bit full scale could reach.

peak_dbfs.description: Peak sample magnitude over the window, in dBFS.

rms_dbfs.description: RMS over the window, in dBFS.

MeterOutput.description: The stereo output keeps both channels as two-element [L, R] arrays; flattening to a scalar would discard information the pipeline already has.

peak_dbfs.description: Peak sample magnitude over the window as [left, right], in dBFS.

rms_dbfs.description: RMS over the window as [left, right], in dBFS.

Measure.description: One measurement session. The state machine carries one writer per transition: the audio ISR owns armed->capturing->captured and every latch retire, the epoch side owns arm, cancel, the sliced analysis and release. `captured` means buffer-complete, not figures-published; `done` means the figures are published.

fail_reason.description: Valid in the failed state, "none" otherwise. generation/overrun are the arm-time latch checks - a config splice or a dropped block landed inside the window; cancelled is the ISR's acknowledgement of an epoch cancel; reclaimed is the epoch's own retire after 1 s with no audio blocks, the one case where the ISR is provably not running.

vector_id.description: The replay vector the session was armed against; null before any session.

figures.description: Null until an analysis pass completes; retained through done and replaced by the next session.

floors.description: Resolvable floors of the 16-bit replay stimulus, stated beside the figures they bound. A figure at its floor means "at least this good". The -140 dB inter-stage requantisation claim is host-proven and deliberately absent here: no 16-bit transport can verify it on-device.

metrics_service_overruns.description: Epochs on which the METRICS checkpoint exceeded its declared 1 ms budget (the sliced analysis is hosted there). Evidence, not an abort: the counter climbing during analysis says the budget declaration needs revisiting.

MeasureFigures.description: One channel's figures from an 8192-sample window: an IEEE 1057 3-parameter sine fit at the declared f0 supplies THD+N and SNR (SNR excludes harmonics 2..10 from the residual; THD+N does not - the two are different numbers by definition), and Hann-windowed Goertzel supplies the harmonic amplitudes and the frequency-response probes.

thd_n_db.description: Residual (noise + distortion) power over the fitted fundamental, dB.

snr_db.description: Fundamental over the residual minus harmonics 2..10, dB.

thd_db.description: Harmonics 2..10 power sum over the fundamental, dBc.

harmonics_dbc.description: Positional: the 2nd through 10th harmonic, dBc. Harmonics at or above fs/2 are dropped from the tail.

probes_dbfs.description: Positional, matching the request's probes array.

id.description: The replay vector to measure against (the corpus under tools/measure_vectors, uploaded via PUT /sd/replays/{id}).

f0_l.description: Left-channel fit frequency in integer Hz; must sit below fs/2 (48 kHz transport).

f0_r.description: Right-channel fit frequency in integer Hz.

probes.description: Frequency-response probe bins in integer Hz, applied to both channels.

Recorder.description: Flight-recorder bank status (aius-recorder-rolling-buffer.md Phase C): board/constant facts and the trigger config once (uniform across every slot by contract), then the per-slot array. active_slot names which slot the next automatic trigger lands in; slots_recycled counts round-robin wraps onto an already-FROZEN slot (an honest wrap count, not a claim about whether the operator pulled it first). Each slot's own data-pull needs (encoding fields are bank-wide): ring_frames, valid_frames, oldest_frame (physical ring index the stream starts at once wrapped), freeze_generation. valid_frames saturates at ring_frames; on an unwrapped ring oldest_frame is 0 and only valid_frames * frame_bytes bytes exist (PSRAM is never zeroed - nothing outside the valid extent is served).

fitted_mb.description: Probed PSRAM size in MB (0/8/16); 0 is the bare board.

active_slot.description: Index into `slots` the recorder is currently RECORDING/POSTROLL/DRAINING into (or the FROZEN slot awaiting an advance deferred by an outstanding read lease on the next one).

slots_recycled.description: Round-robin wraps onto a slot that was already FROZEN, i.e. potentially not yet pulled. Counts wraps, not evidence loss - nothing marks a generation as read.

deferred_epochs.description: Epochs the round-robin has been unable to advance (the documented correctness-over-liveness trade). Without it a stalled bank looks identical to an idle board.

lease_skips.description: Deferrals whose reason was an outstanding read lease on the next slot.

lease_leaks.description: Data reads that found the PREVIOUS read's lease still held and dropped it themselves. Counted by the HTTP dispatcher, not the bank; it should stay 0 forever, so a nonzero value names a terminal that bypasses the response completion hook.

config_pending.description: A config PUT is still waiting on a mid-capture slot; a capture in flight keeps its old config until its next capture.

newest_frozen_slot.description: The slot a GET /api/recorder/data without a slot parameter reads, so a client never guesses it from the slots array. null when nothing is frozen, which is exactly when that read answers 409.

RecorderSlot.description: One bank slot's capture state - the fields that genuinely vary per capture (bank-wide facts live on the parent Recorder document).

sample_rate_hz.description: Rate of the frames actually in THIS slot's ring, taken from its snapshot rather than the build's nominal constant: on an accepted 44.1 kHz stream the constant would state 48000 and every pulled WAV would play about 8.8% fast.

rate_changes.description: Accepted sample-rate changes this capture spans. One scalar cannot describe a ring that crosses a transition, so a non-zero value means sample_rate_hz is true of only the newest frames and the capture should be rejected rather than mislabelled.

gap_count.description: Blocks dropped because staging was full (a mount-class or watchdog-class epoch stall). Recording is gap-honest, not gapless.

stream_end_frame.description: Frames drained into this slot's ring since arm - the stream index one past the newest retained frame. It maps a stream-indexed field onto the pulled WAV, which is the ring unrolled from oldest_frame for valid_frames frames: wav_index = stream_index - (stream_end_frame - valid_frames), and a negative result is a position the ring has already overwritten.

rate_change_count.description: Rate transitions the core counted for this capture. It keeps counting past the four positions rate_change_frames can hold, so a count larger than that array means the positions are incomplete and the capture must be rejected rather than cut.

rate_change_frames.description: Stream frame positions at which the staged rate disagreed with its predecessor - WHERE the transitions are, which rate_change_count alone cannot say. Truncated at four positions.

RecorderTrigger.description: What froze the capture, latched before the state store that published it. which is 'none' until a trigger fires.

at_frame.description: Frames staged when the trigger latched (logical stream position).

RecorderConfig.description: RAM-only trigger configuration; every key required exactly once. The seven booleans are per-trigger enables (the operator is never masked). gr_threshold_db is 0 (disabled) or negative with at most one fraction digit; the linear compare threshold is derived cold on the device. postroll_blocks counts 512-frame blocks from the trigger block inclusive (188 is about 2 s; 0 freezes at the trigger boundary; values above 938 clamp).

governor_trim.description: Freeze when the latency governor cuts the transmit ring back to its target in one audible skip. Default true: the splice is deliberate, but the capture is what says whether it was worth it.

missed_fill.description: Freeze when a transmit interrupt arrives a whole period late and the DMA repeats a stale half. Default true: the repeat advances no underrun counter, so the capture is the only way to hear what the wire carried.

crc_reject.description: Freeze when a compressed access unit fails its own AC-3 / E-AC-3 syncframe CRC and is replaced by silence instead of decoded. Default true: the capture is what says whether the source or the receiver produced the corruption, and it holds the audio either side of the substituted unit.

SdJobError.description: Failure body emitted asynchronously by the SD job, carrying the byte counters it reached before giving up.

received.description: Request body bytes received, in bytes.

written.description: Body bytes written to SD, in bytes.

expected.description: Body length the job expected from Content-Length, in bytes.

SdDiag.description: The storage service's own record: lifetime job counters, the SD adapter's totals, live ownership of the volume, live transfer progress, and the last latched failure. Diagnostic only, and free to read - every value is already latched, so serving it spends no SD primitive. It covers the storage service's job stream only; the replay refill runs on its own job and is reported in replay_diag.

root_jobs.description: Root-initiated jobs started (the boot CONFIG_LOAD, PROBE and USAGE_REFRESH loads), saturating.

busy_refusals.description: HTTP actions refused because a root job owned the volume. The decisive counter for the probe-versus-card question: non-zero says an upload was refused by the contention rule rather than by the card.

drains.description: Jobs whose HTTP owner was discarded and which were advanced to a terminal state one primitive per epoch with no HTTP correlation.

publish_dropped.description: Publication actions acknowledged and discarded because no consumer was registered. A registered consumer that refuses the payload faults the job instead, so this counts only the genuinely unconsumed case.

mounts.description: Every SD.begin() the adapter has performed, so a probe cadence is visible as a rate rather than inferred from the clock.

driver_faults.description: Primitives the card driver itself refused (it returned false).

protocol_faults.description: Primitives the adapter refused to ask the card for at all - the other half of the driver/protocol split.

last_protocol_action.description: The AiusSdActionKind of the last protocol refusal (firmware/lib/aius_sd/include/aius_sd.h).

last_primitive_us.description: Duration of the adapter's most recent SD primitive, in microseconds.

longest_primitive_us.description: Longest single SD primitive since boot, across every job and every owner. It carries no attribution; replay_diag.longest_action is the counterpart that names the action.

sd_mode.description: SDIO transfer mode of the mounted volume; none while no volume is mounted. A mode change drops the mount, so this reads the new mode only after the next mount.

sd_mode_requested.description: SDIO transfer mode the next mount uses (POST /api/sd/mode; not persisted, every boot starts fifo).

open_misses.description: Failed primitives with no card error code (a missing file, for one): the mount is kept and driver_faults is untouched. Never a fault.

absent_mounts.description: Mount attempts that failed with no card inserted (card detect low). Never a fault; about one per second while the card is out.

busy_timeouts.description: 1 s busy-wait expiries in the vendored SDIO driver (BUSY_TIMEOUT_MICROS), the operational meaning of a DMA hang.

hook_calls.description: Every entry to the SD wait hook (between card commands), inside a window or not, whether or not a producer pass ran.

sd_window_nonyield_max_us.description: Longest stretch inside an SD window with no hook in it (window open to first hook, hook return to next hook, last hook to close); time inside a hook, nested pass included, is never counted. Reset by POST /api/clear.

root_state.description: Lifecycle of the most recent root-initiated job: 0 idle, 1 running, 2 complete, 3 failed. An HTTP-owned job never moves it.

http_owned.description: An HTTP action holds the job and no terminal correlated result has been published yet.

draining.description: A job whose HTTP owner was discarded is being advanced to its terminal state.

file_open.description: The adapter is holding the card's one file handle open.

job_kind.description: AiusSdJobKind of the running job (0 probe, 1 config load, 2 usage refresh, 3 upload, 4 download, 5 delete, 6 replay refill).

job_state.description: AiusSdState of the running job - which primitive of the job's state machine is current (firmware/lib/aius_sd/include/aius_sd.h).

upload_supplied.description: Request-body bytes the HTTP transaction has handed DOWN to the job - how much has been consumed off the socket. 0 for every non-upload job kind, and reset per request. Read against job_transferred: supplied advancing while transferred stands still is a card that has stopped accepting writes, which no other counter distinguishes from an idle board.

job_transferred.description: Bytes the job has COMMITTED to the card, for a download as well as an upload.

job_total.description: The job's requested transfer size, so a reader can compute a fraction without knowing Content-Length.

last_failure.description: The last latched failure, or null when none has been latched - so "no failure yet" cannot be misread as a failure with zeroed fields.

SdDiagFailure.description: One failed SD job, latched at the moment of failure so a 500 on the wire can be attributed afterwards. Every field answers a question the failure cannot otherwise be told apart by.

seq.description: Which failure this is - the nth latched since boot. The whole record is null while no failure has been latched, so this is never 0.

at_ms.description: Board uptime in milliseconds at the failure.

owner.description: Who owned the job: 0 none, 1 HTTP, 2 root, 3 drain (an HTTP-owned job whose owner was discarded and which finished on its own).

refused.description: The job never ran: an HTTP action arrived while a root job owned the volume and was refused in-band. True means the contention rule fired, not that the card misbehaved.

job_kind.description: AiusSdJobKind that failed, or - when refused is true - the kind that was running.

job_state.description: AiusSdState the job held at the failure.

fault.description: AiusSdFault: 0 none, 1 invalid request, 2 protocol, 3 capacity, 4 path, 5 overflow, 6 timeout, 7 short I/O, 8 media, 9 open, 10 seek, 11 I/O, 12 install, 13 rollback, 14 publish, 15 cancelled, 16 cleanup, 17 range, 18 not found.

fault_phase.description: The AiusSdPhase the FIRST fault landed in, latched separately because a terminal failure has already moved the live phase on to the cleanup arm. BEGIN separates a mount failure from a write failure from an install rename.

driver_fault.description: The adapter's own word for what went wrong beneath the engine.

adapter_fault.description: The adapter-level fault code carried alongside it.

root_state.description: Root-job lifecycle at the failure, same encoding as sd_diag.root_state - what else owned the volume when it happened.

draining.description: Whether a drain was in progress at the failure.

mounts_in_job.description: SD.begin() calls between this job's start and its failure. A healthy job mounts exactly once, its own; two or more means something remounted the volume underneath it.

longest_primitive_us.description: Longest single primitive within the failed job, in microseconds.

bytes.description: Bytes the job had transferred when it died.

ReplayDiag.description: The replay refill job's own diagnostics, served BESIDE sd_diag rather than inside it. The refill runs on its own job, not the storage service's, so its failures never reach that service's last_failure: before this object existed a refill fault showed only as sd_diag.driver_faults ticking while last_failure described something else entirely. It also times its own primitives so the worst one keeps the action that caused it.

faults.description: Refill jobs that ended in FAIL.

mounts.description: Mount primitives the refill itself performed. Equal to jobs is the signature of a per-job remount, which is how the 1.02 s stall this object was built to explain was identified.

mount_reuses.description: Mount requests the adapter answered from its cached mount. Adapter-global rather than replay-scoped: every consumer's mounts share one cache, and a per-job attribution would claim a precision this counter does not have.

consecutive_faults.description: Consecutive refill faults the replay service is holding. A single fault is survivable; reaching the service's limit stops the replay, which is the one ending an operator cannot infer from a stopped replay alone.

last_primitive_us.description: Duration of the refill's most recent SD primitive, in microseconds, timed around its own call into the adapter.

longest_primitive_us.description: Longest refill primitive, kept together with longest_action so the worst reading names the card action that produced it.

last_fault.description: AiusSdFault of the last failed refill, same encoding as sd_diag.last_failure.fault.

last_fault_phase.description: AiusSdPhase it landed in - which primitive failed.

last_fault_action.description: AiusSdActionKind that was in flight at the fault.

last_fault_driver.description: The driver's own fault word for it.

last_fault_offset_bytes.description: Byte offset within the replay file the fault landed at.

last_fault_loops.description: Which lap of a looping replay it landed on.

last_fault_at_ms.description: Board uptime in milliseconds at that fault.

AudioDiag.description: AUDIO checkpoint diagnostics: the producer's ingress ring, the bounded service that drains it, the decode pipeline's own service counters, and the epoch timing around both. Ingress fields are copied under the same brief interrupt mask the overrun projection uses; everything else is main-thread-owned. POST /api/clear resets the interval counters and rebases the high-water marks to their current levels.

ingress_level_words.description: Words queued in the ingress ring at the read, out of a 8192-word capacity.

ingress_high_water_words.description: Highest ingress level seen since boot or the last clear.

ingress_generation.description: Ingress discontinuity counter published by the producer; the consumer observes it to attribute a discontinuity rather than infer one.

ingress_dropped_chunks.description: 256-word chunks the producer discarded rather than publish.

ingress_drop_overflow.description: Gaps whose cause was a full ring: the producer's reserve found no slot.

ingress_drop_missing_live.description: Gaps recorded because the live source produced no audio block for the slot.

ingress_drop_short_replay.description: Gaps recorded because a replay refill delivered fewer than the 256 words a chunk needs, so the reserved slot was cancelled instead of committed.

source_changes.description: Times the producer recorded a change of audio source (optical carrier to replay, or back).

source_flushes.description: Consumer flushes taken because the source changed.

gap_flushes.description: Consumer flushes taken because a gap was recorded.

checkpoint_calls.description: AUDIO checkpoint invocations - one per runtime epoch.

input_words_consumed.description: Ingress words the service has consumed, at most 4096 per checkpoint.

service_steps_attempted.description: Bounded output work units attempted, at most 8 per checkpoint.

service_steps_committed.description: Those that committed an output block.

service_generation_resets.description: Pipeline resets the service performed because the ingress generation moved under it.

service_requested_resets.description: Pipeline resets the service performed because the epoch asked for one (a replay start, or a debounced carrier relock).

service_max_us.description: Longest AUDIO checkpoint in microseconds. The declared budget is 8000.

service_max_step_us.description: Longest single pipeline service step (decode/DSP/commit) in microseconds. The defect-35 substep attribution: the service loop cannot preempt a step in flight, so a blown budget is one long step or one long ingest, and this pair says which.

service_max_ingest_us.description: Longest single IEC ingest call in microseconds - the parse-side half of the defect-35 substep attribution pair.

service_max_cycles.description: Longest AUDIO checkpoint in DWT cycles at 600 MHz - the cycle-resolution companion to service_max_us.

service_budget_overruns.description: Checkpoints that exceeded the 8 ms budget.

service_last_failure.description: Last non-OK status the audio service retained, as AiusStatus: 0 ok, 1 need-more, 2 unsupported, 3 malformed, 4 truncated, 5 no-space, 6 invalid-arg, 7 refused. Retained rather than fatal - the service keeps streaming through a recoverable failure.

transmit_stops.description: Checkpoints that ended early because the sink reported back-pressure (transmit blocked).

decode_units.description: Access units the deferred service path decoded.

committed_output_blocks.description: Sink calls that committed a block. A refused block advances the decoded item without counting a commit or a failure.

transmit_stalls.description: Sink calls the transmit ring had no space for. The identical PCM descriptor is retained for retry, so a stall costs no second decode.

retained_retries.description: Sink attempts that re-presented such a retained descriptor.

parse_rejects.description: Bursts the IEC 61937 parser refused during ingest.

decode_rejects.description: Decode or slice failures. The burst is skipped and the stream re-locks: a decode error must not gap the wire.

output_drops.description: Sink failures that were neither back-pressure nor a refusal; pending stream state is reset.

au_abandons.description: Access units abandoned part-decoded, which for a multi-block unit is the difference between one lost block and one lost unit.

pipeline_last_failure.description: The pipeline service's last non-OK status, same AiusStatus encoding as service_last_failure.

tx_level_frames.description: Frames queued in the S/PDIF transmit ring at the read.

tx_high_water_frames.description: Highest transmit-ring level since boot or the last clear, which rebases it to the current level rather than to zero.

runtime_epoch_max_us.description: Longest complete runtime epoch in microseconds - the whole loop, not just AUDIO. The declared budget is 25000.

runtime_epoch_budget_overruns.description: Epochs that exceeded the 25 ms budget.

producer_wait_passes.description: Nested producer passes run from the SD wait hook inside an SD window.

producer_point_passes.description: Nested producer passes run from a checkpoint yield point (every boundary except EPOCH_COMPLETE).

producer_pend_latency_max_us.description: Longest wait from an unserved ingress commit to the next producer pass start, in microseconds. Reset by POST /api/clear.

producer_late_passes.description: Passes whose pend latency exceeded D (2,500 us). Reset by POST /api/clear.

stack_free_min_bytes.description: Since-boot floor of untouched DTCM stack (boot paint, scanned at 1 Hz). Not reset by POST /api/clear.

Clock.description: The authoritative sample-rate-following surface: what the receiver measured, what the transmitter was actually programmed to, and the counters that say how the two got there. The legacy top-level sample_rate stays beside it and still means the rounded carrier measurement. Counters are cleared by POST /api/clear.

carrier_locked.description: The latched receiver lock, the same input tx_gate.carrier_locked reports - taken from the epoch's decision rather than re-read here.

carrier_ready.description: The rate tracker has a settled, supported carrier rate a clock plan can be built from.

carrier_rate_millihz.description: Measured carrier rate in millihertz, so 48021000 is 48.021 kHz. Millihertz because parts-per-million of 48 kHz is tens of millihertz and an integer hertz field would quantise the whole measurement away.

nominal_rate_hz.description: Nominal programme rate the output is running at: the tracked carrier nominal, or the 48000 build constant while the output is master.

stream_rate_hz.description: Sample rate of the last block the decode path published - a property of the programme, not a measurement of the wire.

output_rate_millihz.description: Rate the transmitter is actually clocked at, in millihertz, after the applied PLL trim.

trim_ppm.description: output_rate_millihz against nominal_rate_hz in parts per million. Signed, and 0 when no nominal is known.

master.description: "input" while the transmitter follows the carrier; "output" while the board's own clock is master, which is the replay case.

state.description: First match wins, in this order: "replay" the output is master; "fault" a clock apply failed and the episode has not cleared; "unlocked" no carrier is locked; "unsupported" the carrier's rate is outside the supported set (32000, 44100, 48000); then with a settled carrier "tracking" when the plan is applied and "refused" when it is not; "acquiring" while the tracker is still settling.

rate_changes.description: Accepted changes of nominal programme rate. Each one also emits an event.

trim_updates.description: Centre commits: every centre the rate tracker commits, including commits that write nothing and structural replans (clock_note_centre_commit). Use centre_writes for accepted CENTRE writes. Since 2026-09-07 a same-nominal trim opens NO validity window: the numerator step is carrier-continuous, so the four-period V=1 hold it used to raise (a mute on a validity-honouring DAC) is gone and invalid_windows no longer counts trims.

trim_last_at_ms.description: millis() at the last accepted trim REQUEST, so a heard glitch can be placed against it. Lifetime: POST /api/clear zeroes trim_updates and leaves this, because when the last trim happened stays true. 0 = none this boot.

trim_applied_at_ms.description: millis() at the TX period boundary that actually wrote CCM_ANALOG_PLL_AUDIO_NUM for a CENTRE trim (a carrier-estimate retarget), stamped in the transmit ISR. With trim_last_at_ms it brackets the queueing delay, which is at most one 128-frame period (2.67 ms). A FILL trim stamps fill_applied_at_ms instead. 0 = no centre trim applied this boot.

fill_offset_millihz.description: The fill loop's signed offset: the composed output-rate target minus the centre (the carrier-estimate target), in millihertz, clamped to +/-900. Positive speeds the output up (the ring is filling). Updated every rate-service pass; 0 before the first lock and after a reset of the loop (accept, full apply, replay, carrier loss).

fill_setpoint_frames.description: This lock's fill setpoint in frames: the phase-corrected occupancy measured inside the gate open's masked section, 384 - phi*128 (257 to 384). When a period boundary was pending the open pads one more half, which the late ISR takes on the unmask, so the setpoint is 384 - phi'*128 in the same range. Fixed for the lock; a governor trim leaves it valid. 0 = no live open yet, after carrier loss or a rate change, and for a replay open.

fill_open_boundary_pending.description: Whether the last live gate open saw a pending period boundary: true when the TX DMA already read the half the ISR last filled, so the open padded one extra half (gate_open_pending_padded_frames) and fill_setpoint_frames is 384 - phi'*128, phi' read in the new half; false for 384 - phi*128. Both give 257 to 384. Carrier loss and a rate change clear it with the setpoint.

fill_trims.description: Accepted FILL trim requests: carrier-continuous numerator writes from the fill loop, at most one per fill window. POST /api/clear zeroes it. A centre retarget's write counts in centre_writes instead.

centre_writes.description: Accepted CENTRE trim requests: carrier-continuous numerator writes that land a committed centre. POST /api/clear zeroes it. Not bounded per fill window: a FILL write and a CENTRE write may share one.

fill_trim_last_at_ms.description: millis() at the last accepted FILL trim REQUEST. Lifetime, like trim_last_at_ms. 0 = none this boot.

fill_applied_at_ms.description: millis() at the TX period boundary that wrote the numerator for a FILL trim, stamped in the transmit ISR. With fill_trim_last_at_ms it brackets the queueing delay (at most one 128-frame period). 0 = no fill trim applied this boot.

structural_replans.description: Target updates whose plan was NOT structurally equal to the applied one, so a full plan apply was selected instead of a trim.

invalid_windows.description: Advanced by the clock-apply path, once per successful plan apply. Despite the name the firmware does not increment it for a rejected tracker window (optical_main.cpp clock_apply_desired_plan and clock_service); it is documented as it behaves rather than as it reads. It stopped counting accepted trim requests on 2026-09-07, when a trim stopped opening a validity window at all - see trim_updates.

clock_faults.description: Clock fault EPISODES, not failed attempts: a fault latches the episode and repeated failures inside it do not count again.

last_clock_fault.description: The last apply result recorded as a fault: 0 ok, 1 invalid plan (the requested rate has no representable PLL plan), 2 lock timeout (the PLL did not lock inside the bound).

mismatch_blocks.description: Blocks refused because their sample rate was not the rate the output is currently programmed for. The gate closes and the block is dropped rather than played at the wrong rate.

unsupported_blocks.description: Blocks refused because their sample rate is outside the supported set (32000, 44100, 48000).

unsupported_episodes.description: Runs of such blocks, counted once per episode rather than once per block. Each one also emits an event.

tx_level_frames.description: Frames queued in the S/PDIF transmit ring at the read, the same reading audio_diag.tx_level_frames carries.

tx_underrun_frames.description: Lifetime frames the transmit ISR had to invent because the ring was empty WHILE THE TX GATE WAS OPEN. Closed-gate (idle/dark) substitution is not counted, so the value is a true audible-glitch metric rather than a free-running idle counter. It survives the ring flush a rate change performs, so a rate transition cannot hide its own underrun. underrun_episodes below places its advances in time.

tx_missed_fills.description: Transmit interrupts that arrived a whole 128-frame period (2.67 ms) late, detected by the ISR filling the same DMA half twice in a row. The DMA had already re-transmitted the stale half, so this is an audible REPEAT that advances no underrun counter. An even number of missed periods restores the half parity and is invisible here; the level instruments carry that case. Cleared by nothing.

tx_missed_fill_frames.description: Frames the ISR dropped from the ring to undo a missed fill's standing cost. Each miss leaves one AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES of occupancy no fill consumed - permanent extra latency the governor would otherwise cut with a second audible skip seconds later - so the ISR advances the consumer cursor by that much immediately.

tx_missed_fill_at_ms.description: millis() at the newest missed fill. 0 = none this boot.

tx_missed_fill_flexspi_intr.description: FLEXSPI_INTR sampled at the FIRST miss of the newest burst (the thread releases the snapshot when it publishes the event, so a later burst overwrites it). A missed transmit interrupt is a latency fault and the prime suspect on this board is a FlexSPI bus hold - program flash is XIP on FlexSPI1. Raw word: the host decodes, the firmware stays a camera.

tx_missed_fill_flexspi2_intr.description: FLEXSPI2_INTR at the same instant - the bus the recorder's PSRAM sits on.

tx_missed_fill_flexspi2_sts1.description: FLEXSPI2_STS1 at the same instant: the controller's last command/latency status, which is what says whether the hold was a PSRAM access.

gate_open_target_frames.description: The compile-time transmit-ring occupancy every closed-to-open gate edge sets the ring to (e2e-latency Phase 3 R1; output-jitter Phase F). The edge executes at the producer's pre-commit instant and trims down or pads up with silence, so the standing pre-commit floor of a session is exactly this constant rather than the phase luck of the first burst; 256 is two blocks of service-jitter margin beyond the in-flight block, the deployed env runs 128.

gate_open_replay_target_frames.description: The compile-time transmit-ring occupancy a gate-open edge sets when the source is a replay (2026-09-03). A replay's producer is the SD refill job, whose OPEN_READ / READ primitives (8.3 / 6.3 ms measured) block the epoch two checkpoints before AUDIO enqueues, so the live target's one block of margin lost that race at replay start about one run in three. Replay has no lip-sync to protect, so its floor is sized to the primitive: the deployed env runs 768 (16 ms). A replay start therefore advances gate_open_padded_frames by up to this value, not gate_open_target_frames; a replay-to-live relock trims back to the live target.

gate_open_trims.description: Gate-open edges that actually dropped frames to reach the target. Dropping at this edge is inaudible by construction - the gate was closed, the output dark.

gate_open_trimmed_frames.description: Lifetime frames dropped by gate-open trims. Together with tx_underrun_frames this is the acceptance instrument for the target value: a target set too low shows up as post-open underruns, too high as latency.

gate_open_last_trim_at_ms.description: millis() at the last gate-open edge that actually dropped frames, so a relock can be placed against a heard glitch. No frames field beside it: this edge's drop is inaudible by construction (the pad was dark) and its size is already summed in gate_open_trimmed_frames. 0 = no trimming edge this boot.

gate_open_padded_frames.description: Lifetime frames of silence the gate-open edge committed to lift a short ring up to gate_open_target_frames (output-jitter Phase F). Unheard by construction - the pad was still dark. A relock empties the ring, so a relock pads up to a full target's worth (nothing when the producer's first burst happened to leave exactly the target at the open instant); the invariant is the floor, not the pad size.

gate_open_pending_padded_frames.description: Lifetime frames of silence a live gate open padded above gate_open_target_frames because a TX period boundary was pending at the open (aius-sample-rate-following Phase 4a F3): up to one half, 128 frames, per such open, counting only frames actually padded (a ring already above the target pads less, and one at or above target plus 128 trims instead, counted in gate_open_trimmed_frames). The masked boundary ISR takes that half on the unmask, so the level after it is the target and the fill setpoint is 384 - phi'*128 as in the normal case. Counted apart from gate_open_padded_frames, which still advances by at most one target per live relock.

governor_trims.description: Gate-OPEN trims by the latency governor (aius-output-jitter Phase E): a stall backlog that parked the ring's standing floor a sustained window above gate_open_target_frames was cut back to the target in one audible skip. Zero in a stall-free session.

governor_trimmed_frames.description: Lifetime frames the governor dropped. Each trim's size is the measured floor excess over the gate-open target, so trimmed_frames/trims is the mean ratchet the session suffered.

governor_last_trim_at_ms.description: millis() at the last governor trim. The two lifetime totals say a splice happened this boot; this says when, which is what places it against a glitch the owner heard. 0 = none this boot.

governor_last_trim_frames.description: Frames that one trim dropped, i.e. the size of the last audible skip. The totals' mean cannot distinguish one 2000-frame cut from ten 200-frame ones.

ingress_level_words.description: Ingress ring level at the read, repeated here so the clock story reads without cross-referencing audio_diag.

underrun_episode_count.description: Lifetime gate-open underrun EPISODES that have ended. underrun_episodes holds the newest 8; anything above 8 here has been overwritten. An episode still open is in neither number until it ends.

fill_level_q4.description: Phase-corrected transmit-ring occupancy, the last valid 192,000-frame window statistic, in 1/16 frame (level + 256 minus the DMA read offset in frames, minimum per 12,000-frame sub-window, mean of the non-excluded minima). Signed. null before the first valid window, after a reset (gate close, governor trim, carrier loss, replay block) and after a closed window with fewer than 8 valid sub-windows, until the next valid window closes. Observed only; nothing acts on it.

fill_subwindow_spread_frames.description: Max minus min of the sub-window minima behind the last valid fill_level_q4, in frames. 0 whenever fill_level_q4 is null (before the first valid window, after a reset, after an invalid window).

fill_windows.description: Valid fill windows published (at least 8 of 16 sub-windows valid). Lifetime.

fill_subwindows_excluded.description: Sub-windows excluded from the fill statistic (an underrun, a missed fill, a production stall, or no sample). Lifetime.

fill_torn_reads.description: Fill samples dropped after three torn reads of the ring's fills counter. Lifetime.

fill_window_seq.description: Closed fill windows, valid or not (fill_windows counts valid ones only), so a reader sees every close. Lifetime; survives a sensor reset; wraps at 2^32.

fill_window_exclusions.description: Exclusion-reason bits ORed over the last closed window's sub-windows: 1 underrun, 2 production stall, 4 missed fill, 8 no sample. 0 after a sensor reset (gate close, governor trim, carrier loss, replay block).

underrun_episodes.description: The newest eight underrun episodes, OLDEST FIRST. tx_underrun_frames is a boot-lifetime total with no timestamp, so it can say a glitch happened between two polls but never when, how long, or whether one poll interval held one burst or thirty. Each episode groups the counter's consecutive advances at the accepted-block cadence (~10.7 ms at 48 kHz), which is coarser than the transmit ISR's own 2.67 ms fill period, so one stall coalesces into one episode instead of fragmenting per fill.

UnderrunEpisode.description: One run of gate-open transmit underrun. Posted to the event ring as type 14 when it ends.

start_ms.description: millis() at the observation that opened the episode. The underrun itself happened somewhere in the service interval before it, so the stamp is accurate to one accepted block rather than to the frame.

ms.description: Span from that observation to the last one that still carried an advance - the OBSERVED extent, which is 0 for a burst contained inside a single service pass. Read frames for the audible cost; a 128-frame episode reading ms 0 is one 2.7 ms glitch reported honestly, not a lost measurement.

frames.description: Frames of silence the transmit ISR substituted during the episode. frames / sample rate is the silence a listener heard, exact whatever ms says.

gate_open.description: 1 = the episode ended with the gate still open, i.e. the stream recovered. 0 = a gate close ended it, so its extent is truncated and the drain transient a stop or relock causes is deliberately not counted into it.

ClkRegs.description: Raw S/PDIF + audio-PLL clock-tree registers, read at request time - the boot-lottery discriminator (aius-open-work-register.md, open defects / runtime). The degraded mode's hypothesis is a clock tree latched wrong at boot while every in-domain surface self-reports 48 kHz; these words are served as hex strings, undecoded, so the report cannot be fooled by the clock it reports on. The diff between a degraded boot and the same board after its warm-reboot flip convicts or acquits the chain.

spdif_srpc.description: SPDIF_SRPC: receiver clock-recovery control and the DPLL LOCK bit (bit 6). CLKSRC_SEL and GAINSEL are the fields the receiver-engine-clock hypothesis turns on.

spdif_stc.description: SPDIF_STC: transmit clock control. Nominal for this image is TXCLK_SOURCE 1 (tx_clk from SPDIF0_CLK_ROOT) with TXCLK_DF 27.

spdif_srfm.description: SPDIF_SRFM frequency measurement - the DPLL's own carrier-rate reading, the input to clock.carrier_rate_millihz. Treat with suspicion: on junk-locked boots this word held a stale value bit-identical to healthy boots while the engines demonstrably crawled, so it can fossilize rather than measure.

spdif_sis.description: SPDIF_SIS interrupt status word. Since the input-fault instruments (pop diagnosis 2026-08-16), the error subset (BITERR, SYMERR, LOCKLOSS, RxFIFO under/overrun and resync) is counted and W1C-cleared once per epoch by input_fault_service(), so those bits here are at most one epoch old - the accumulated history lives in input_diag. All other bits remain unmanaged.

pll_audio.description: CCM_ANALOG_PLL_AUDIO. Nominal for the 48 kHz tree is DIV_SELECT 28, ENABLE set, BYPASS and POWERDOWN clear. (set_audioClock() silently keeps a pre-enabled PLL whatever its frequency; the 2026-08-02 investigation acquitted that seam - degraded boots dump nominal words here - and convicted the receiver DPLL's junk lock instead, see relocks.)

pll_audio_num.description: CCM_ANALOG_PLL_AUDIO_NUM - nominal 6720 before trim; the sample-rate follower writes this word live, so small deviations are trim, not corruption.

misc2.description: CCM_ANALOG_MISC2 - the audio post-divider bits live here; nominal has both clear.

cdcdr.description: CCM_CDCDR - SPDIF0 clock mux and dividers; nominal is CLK_SEL 0 (PLL4), PRED 7, PODF 0 (divide by 8 overall).

ccgr5.description: CCM_CCGR5 - carries the SPDIF clock gate.

spdif_in_master.description: 1 when the S/PDIF receiver's DMA interrupt holds AudioStream update responsibility (the input paces the graph). The input and output flags are separate per-class statics; serving both is what proves neither or both hold it.

spdif_out_master.description: 1 when the transmitter's DMA interrupt paces the graph instead (replay clock handover).

tx_fills.description: Transmit-DMA fill passes since boot, one per AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES wire frames. Against wall time this is the TX bit clock measured from outside the S/PDIF clock domain - the counter a self-consistently wrong clock tree cannot fool.

relocks.description: Boot-time S/PDIF DPLL re-acquisitions the boot-lottery gate performed: the engine rate is cross-checked against the DWT clock after audio bring-up and the S/PDIF core soft-reset until the rates agree. 0 is a boot that verified healthy first try; 1-4 is a junk-locked boot the gate cured; a value pinned at 5 is a boot the gate could not cure (alive, dark, and named here).

PollProbe.description: The retained fnet_poll probe - the diagnostic vector for the periodic DHCP-T1 watchdog wedge (aius-open-work-register.md, open defects / runtime). fnet_poll is not reentrant and the port's FNET mutexes are no-ops, yet the historic model ran it from a 1 kHz timer ISR while main-loop server code also polled inline. Storage survives watchdog resets in the ldscript's .aius_retained window, so the boot after a wedge serves the dying boot's record.

wedges.description: Boots that died inside fnet_poll since the probe was last power-cycled clean (sticky; each new wedge overwrites ctx/dhcp/depth below).

ctx.description: Caller context of the most recent fatal entry: 1 timer ISR, 2 NativeEthernetServer main-loop spin, 3 network-job poll (single-context model); 0 no wedge recorded.

dhcp.description: FNET DHCP-client state at the fatal entry (fnet_dhcp_cln state enum; 5 BOUND, 6 RENEWING). 255 = no DHCP descriptor existed.

depth.description: Poll nesting depth the dying boot left behind; nonzero is what marks the death as inside fnet_poll.

prev_maxd.description: Previous boot's poll-depth high-water; 2 or more proves fnet_poll re-entered.

prev_reent.description: Previous boot's count of reentrant poll entries.

reent.description: This boot's live reentrant-entry count, the fastest on-device confirmation that the split polling model actually re-enters.

InputDiag.description: The input-fault instruments (pop diagnosis 2026-08-16): three independent watermarks that attribute an audible underrun burst. The SIS latch counts the SPDIF peripheral's sticky physical-layer error flags per epoch window and clears them, so an error is attributable to its window rather than 'since boot'; the production-gap watermark times the hole itself whatever its cause; the update-ISR cadence watermark convicts or acquits the in-firmware loss path (RX DMA overwrite during ISR starvation). Emitted by http_input_diag_json (optical_main.cpp).

sis_biterr_events.description: Epoch windows in which the SPDIF receiver latched a biphase-mark coding bit error (SIS BITERR). A window is ~ms, so this approximates error events, not error bits.

sis_symerr_events.description: Epoch windows with a latched symbol error (SIS SYMERR).

sis_lockloss_events.description: Epoch windows with a latched momentary lock loss (SIS LOCKLOSS). Catches losses too brief for the software relock counter to ever observe.

sis_rxfifo_events.description: Epoch windows with a latched RX FIFO under/overrun or resync (SIS RXFIFOUNOV | RXFIFORESYN).

sis_last_error_ms.description: millis() of the most recent window that latched any counted SIS error; 0 when none has.

production_gap_max_us.description: Longest observed micros() between two ACCEPTED producer blocks with the TX gate open. Steady PCM runs ~10.7 ms, AC-3 ~32 ms per sync frame; a lost burst doubles the AC-3 figure.

production_gap_alert_us.description: The compile-time alert threshold (AIUS_INPUT_GAP_ALERT_US, default 40000): one AC-3 sync-frame period plus margin, so only a real hole alerts.

production_gap_over_count.description: Production gaps that exceeded the alert threshold. Each audible pop should pair with exactly one increment here; an increment without a pop means the ring cushion absorbed the hole.

production_gap_last_us.description: Size of the most recent over-threshold gap.

production_gap_last_at_ms.description: millis() of the most recent over-threshold gap - correlate with sis_last_error_ms to attribute it.

update_gap_max_us.description: Longest observed micros() between audio update ISR calls (nominal ~2667). A maximum approaching the RX DMA buffering depth is the in-firmware input-loss signature; a nominal value at a pop acquits the firmware side.

rx_dropped_halves.description: Lifetime S/PDIF receive DMA halves dropped because the AudioStream block pair was still unconsumed or unallocated (aius_spdif_rx.h). Advances in practice only while replay drives the graph with the receiver's DPLL unlocked, when the receive DMA storms at several times the block rate; the retained vendor ISR wrote those halves past the block pair instead (RX pool corruption under replay, 2026-09-03).

pool_blocks_used.description: AudioStream blocks in use right now, out of the 24 AudioMemory() allocates. Steady state is at most 4 (the receive pair being filled plus the pair in flight to the processor); a higher floor that never returns is a leaked or corrupted pool, whose symptom is ingress_drop_missing_live advancing with the carrier locked.

dark_alert_ms.description: The compile-time over-count threshold for a gate-closed phase run (AIUS_INPUT_DARK_ALERT_MS, default 3000): the plan's steady-phase dark-with-carrier bound. A legitimate acquisition is honestly ~1.5 s (8 tracker samples over 1 s plus a ~170 ms confirmation or starvation window), so only a run past this is over-counted.

dark_record_min_ms.description: The compile-time floor for recording a dark interval (AIUS_INPUT_DARK_RECORD_MIN_MS, default 500). An AC-3 sync frame is ~32 ms apart and the worst legitimate E-AC-3 outcome gap ~256 ms, so intervals under this floor are codec cadence, not the box.

dark_phase.description: The transmit gate's ladder position this epoch, tested in the firmware's own guard order: 0 no_carrier (receiver PLL unlocked), 1 rate_unsupported (locked at a rate the tracker refused; stuck state 3), 2 clock_acquiring (tracker has not accepted a nominal), 3 plan_pending (nominal accepted, output plan not applied), 4 awaiting_block (plan applied, no decoded block has cleared enqueue's guards; stuck states 1 and 2 park here), 5 gate_armed (a block landed and armed the open, the producer has not executed it), 6 gate_open. Observe-only: nothing acts on it (aius-input-recovery Phase 1).

dark_phase_ms.description: How long dark_phase has held, ms. While a box is stuck this is the live reading; the phase's watermark row only latches when the run ends.

dark_open.description: 1 while a dark interval is open: no output block has committed since dark_open_start_ms.
