An interval runs from the last epoch that committed a block to the next one that does (the input-liveness boundary), so production stopping under an OPEN gate is an interval like any other.

dark_open_ms.description: How long the open dark interval has run, ms, timed from the last commit; 0 when dark_open is 0.

dark_open_start_ms.description: millis() of the last commit before the open interval; 0 when dark_open is 0.

dark_open_entry_phase.description: dark_phase at the epoch the open interval was entered (dark_phase's vocabulary). Meaningful only while dark_open is 1.

dark_open_entry_class.description: Pipeline class at entry: 0 unknown, 1 PCM, 2 IEC 61937 non-linear (the DTS/AC-3/E-AC-3 path), the same AiusPipelineClass pipeline_diag.class carries.

dark_open_entry_ready.description: Whether the rate tracker had accepted a nominal at entry (clock.carrier_ready).

dark_open_entry_gate.description: Whether the physical transmit gate was open at entry. 1 here is the class-latched-silent shape: production stopped with the gate still open.

dark_interval_count.description: Lifetime count of recorded dark intervals (those at or past dark_record_min_ms). dark_intervals holds the newest 8; anything above 8 here has been overwritten.

dark_phases.description: The gate-closed companion to the production-gap watermark: one row per gate-closed ladder phase (dark_phase 0..5, in that order), each timing its contiguous runs. The production-gap watermark resets whenever the gate is closed, by design, so every stuck state lives in the region these rows measure. Hours with the entertainment stack off land in row 0 (no_carrier) and nowhere else.

dark_intervals.description: The newest recorded dark intervals, oldest first, each with the ladder phase, pipeline class, tracker acceptance and physical gate at entry and at exit. A fixed ring of 8; dark_interval_count says how many it has overwritten.

InputDarkPhase.description: One gate-closed ladder phase's run watermark (aius-input-recovery Phase 1). A run is a contiguous stretch of epochs in this phase; it latches here when the phase moves. Same shape as production_gap_*: max, over-threshold count, and the most recent over-threshold run.

phase.description: The row's phase, in InputDiag.dark_phase's vocabulary (6 gate_open has no row: that region is the production gap's).

max_ms.description: Longest completed run in this phase, ms.

last_ms.description: Duration of the most recent over-threshold run; 0 when none has occurred.

last_at_ms.description: millis() at which the most recent over-threshold run ended; 0 when none has occurred.

InputDarkInterval.description: One recorded dark interval: from the last epoch that committed an output block to the next one that did, with the box's state at both ends. An interval that exited with exit_gate 1 and exit_ready 1 recovered; the entry snapshot says what it looked like when production stopped.

start_ms.description: millis() of the last commit before the interval.

ms.description: Duration to the commit that closed it, ms; at least InputDiag.dark_record_min_ms.

entry_phase.description: InputDiag.dark_phase at the first epoch without a commit.

exit_phase.description: InputDiag.dark_phase at the epoch that observed the closing commit.

PrevBoot.description: The previous boot's retained forensics, captured before aius_boot_init folds the ledger away. These were CDC-only (`pv=` / `fa=` on the USB ID line) until the 2026-08-16 slot-trial fallback showed the one moment they matter most is exactly when the board is deployed and USB is a room away.

final_checkpoint.description: The last checkpoint (0-10) the previous boot persisted before it died - for a watchdog-killed boot, the checkpoint it starved in. 65535 when the retained ledger was invalid (first boot after power-on, or corruption).

first_abort.description: The previous boot's FIRST aborting checkpoint (defect 25's one-shot latch): the service whose false return started a starvation. 0-9 a checkpoint, 254 no abort, 255 latch invalid.

FaultRecord.description: The most recent CPU fault, as the core's fault handler recorded it. return_address is the stacked PC - decode host-side with addr2line against the faulting build's ELF. CFSR/HFSR name the fault class (data access violation, bus fault, usage fault); MMFAR/BFAR carry the offending address when their valid bits are set in CFSR.

ipsr.description: Exception number active at the fault (0 = thread mode).

cfsr.description: Configurable Fault Status Register, 8-digit hex - the memory-management / bus / usage fault class bits.

hfsr.description: HardFault Status Register, 8-digit hex - FORCED set means an escalated configurable fault.

mmfar.description: MemManage fault address, 8-digit hex; meaningful only when CFSR.MMARVALID is set. Below 32 is the nullptr signature.

bfar.description: Bus fault address, 8-digit hex; meaningful only when CFSR.BFARVALID is set.

return_address.description: Stacked program counter at the fault, 8-digit hex - the addr2line input.

xpsr.description: Stacked xPSR at the fault, 8-digit hex.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since boot when the fault hit.

StallDiag.description: The stall witness's verdict object for the ~1.79 s global-stall family (aius-open-work-register.md, open defects / runtime). A GPT1 heartbeat at NVIC priority 0 ticks 1 kHz; across any epoch over 100 ms the loop compares wall time against the witness's tick advance. A deficit near the whole stall says nothing below priority 0 ran - an interrupts-masked section or a bus-level hold - while a deficit near zero says the witness lived through it, and its NVIC IABR snapshot names the ISR it kept preempting. The 2026-08-03 measurement that motivated it: nine of eleven checkpoint_walltime_us maxima within ±22 us of 2^30 CPU cycles (1,789,570 us), i.e. random-phase CPU theft, not a slow service.

events.description: Epochs since boot whose wall time exceeded the 100 ms witness threshold.

last_us.description: Wall time of the most recent stalled epoch in microseconds (the 1.79 s family reads ~1,790,000 here).

last_deficit_ms.description: Witness ticks missing across the last stalled epoch, in milliseconds of silence below NVIC priority 0. ~= last_us/1000: masked-interrupts or bus hold; ~0: an ISR spin the witness survived.

max_deficit_ms.description: Largest tick deficit any stalled epoch has shown since boot.

witness_ticks.description: Lifetime 1 kHz witness ticks; against uptime this proves the witness itself is alive and its priority intact.

isr_samples.description: Stall episodes the witness observed from inside - it fired during a stale heartbeat window and captured the IABR snapshot. Zero while events advances is itself the bus-hold/masked verdict.

iabr.description: NVIC_IABR words 0-4 (IRQs 0-159 active bits) captured at the first witness tick inside the most recent observed episode, 8-digit lowercase hex. A set bit names an interrupt handler that was running (or preempted) while the main loop starved.

pc.description: The preempted context's stacked program counter, captured with the IABR snapshot on the episode's first witness tick, 8-digit lowercase hex. Decode host-side with addr2line against the build's ELF: this is the exact instruction the stall was spinning at.

lr.description: The preempted context's stacked link register from the same exception frame - the spinning function's caller when pc alone is ambiguous (leaf spins, shared helpers).

flexspi_intr.description: FLEXSPI_INTR raw word read after the last stalled epoch, 8-digit lowercase hex. Bit 10 AHBBUSTIMEOUT and bit 11 SEQTIMEOUT are the flash-side bus-stall tell.

flexspi2_intr.description: FLEXSPI2_INTR raw word read after the last stalled epoch, 8-digit lowercase hex - the PSRAM-side controller, the prime suspect surface for the fabric-hold hypothesis.

flexspi2_sts1.description: FLEXSPI2_STS1 raw word read after the last stalled epoch, 8-digit lowercase hex. AHBCMDERRID (bits 3:0) names the AHB buffer/master whose command errored and AHBCMDERRCODE (bits 11:8) the error class - the register that says WHO issued the timing-out PSRAM access.

ReplayList.description: GET /api/replays listing. Bounded enumeration of /aius/replays: complete vectors (.iec) and in-flight uploads (.part) only; other files are skipped silently. truncated:true means either the scan cap or the response buffer stopped the listing early - the rows present are correct, the set is incomplete.

bytes.description: Current on-card size (.part: bytes staged so far).

duration_seconds.description: bytes / 192,000 (48 kHz stereo s16 IEC61937 wire rate) for a complete vector; null for a .part.

upload_next_offset.description: Resume offset for a chunked upload - equals bytes; the uploader appends from here.

active.description: true when this complete vector is the replay service's current selection.

ReplayStatus.description: GET /api/replays/status. The replay service's live record. state is the portable service's own vocabulary; stop_reason says who stopped it (carrier = a live input reclaimed the path, request = POST /api/replays/stop, fault = the service stopped itself) and reads none while anything other than stopped.

queue_words.description: IEC words queued toward the decoder.

refill_faults.description: SD refill job faults; the replay_diag object on GET /api/status carries the fault detail.

PipelineDiag.description: The decode pipeline's own record: the classifier's verdict, the resident decoders' metrics, and the faults deferred service swallows. Deferred service skips a faulted burst and keeps streaming - a decode error must not gap the wire - which is exactly why a silent decoder was once invisible from every surface: classified, zero output, and its last status trapped in RAM.

class.description: Classifier verdict: 0 undecided (fewer than the classification window's words and no preamble yet), 1 IEC 60958 linear PCM (a full window with no preamble), 2 IEC 61937 non-linear (a preamble pair was found).

codec_pc.description: The IEC 61937 Pc (data-type) word the pipeline latched from the last decoded burst; 0 before one.

metrics_valid.description: 1 when the metrics read below answered. 0 only when the pipeline never constructed, so every metric beside it is a zero that means "not measured".

last_status.description: The decoder's last status, as AiusStatus (0 ok, 1 need-more, 2 unsupported, 3 malformed, 4 truncated, 5 no-space, 6 invalid-arg, 7 refused).

create_status.description: The status the pipeline's construction returned, same encoding. Anything but 0 means there is no pipeline at all, which is a different failure from a pipeline that decodes badly.

decode_cycles.description: DWT cycles of the last decode on the shared metrics view; 0 on a host build, which has no cycle counter.

arena_high_water.description: Codec-slot high-water in bytes: peak decoder memory across every slot residency so far (one decoder exists at a time; a Pc family change resets the slot and creates the other decoder into it).

alloc_count.description: Allocations on the last decode path. 0 is the expected value; a non-zero count means the decode path allocated.

dts_decode_cycles.description: The DTS decoder's own last-decode cycles, read separately so the shared view above cannot hide which codec ran. All-zero when DTS is not the slot resident (a non-resident codec's state left with the slot).

dts_alloc_count.description: The DTS decoder's allocation count; 0 when DTS is not the slot resident.

ac3_decode_cycles.description: The AC-3 decoder's own last-decode cycles; all-zero when AC-3 is not the slot resident.

ac3_alloc_count.description: The AC-3 decoder's allocation count; 0 when AC-3 is not the slot resident.

eac3_decode_cycles.description: The E-AC-3 decoder's own last-decode cycles; all-zero when E-AC-3 is not the slot resident - and always zero until the AIUS_PIPELINE_EAC3 route is compiled into the image (E-AC-3 plan phase 4).

eac3_alloc_count.description: The E-AC-3 decoder's allocation count; 0 when E-AC-3 is not the slot resident, and always zero until phase 4 compiles the route in.

decode_rejects.description: Decode or slice failures recorded by the pipeline service - the same counter audio_diag.decode_rejects carries.

crc_rejects.description: Compressed access units refused by their own AC-3 / E-AC-3 syncframe CRC before any decode ran, and replaced by silence at the cadence the decode would have produced. Neither a decode_reject (no decoder was called) nor an au_abandon (the class, the audio generation and the transmit ring all survive). A climbing count with decode_rejects and au_abandons flat means the source is delivering complete-but-corrupt frames - the receiver micro-flap case - not that the board is failing.

crc_reject_last_at_ms.description: Device millis() at the most recent CRC reject; 0 when none has happened this boot. The stamp is what places a heard crackle against the counter.

rejects_no_space.description: Bursts refused because the payload did not fit.

rejects_malformed.description: Bursts refused as malformed (sync, length or CRC).

rejects_unsupported.description: Bursts that were well-formed but out of scope for the resident decoders.

resyncs.description: Returns to preamble search from a non-terminal parser state.

last_reject_pc.description: The NORMALISED Pc header word of the most recent malformed or no-space burst. Reading it beside last_reject_pd answers byte order, bit slips, or genuine garbage in one look.

last_reject_pd.description: The normalised Pd header word of that same burst.

retype_count.description: Lifetime re-types of the stream. On a live board a non-zero value is what distinguishes a mid-stream re-type from a reboot that happened to classify the other way.

squelched_frames.description: Frames dropped by the PCM confirmation squelch. Advancing while pcm_confirmed is 0 is the signature of a mis-typed run being dropped rather than played - the seam that used to be audible as periodic buzz.

pcm_confirmed.description: 1 once the PCM classification has been confirmed and the squelch has opened.

BootFuse.description: The boot-configuration fuse word 0x6E0, hex-encoded with its two decoded fields. Whether the part has these bits blown is the single gating fact for hardware A/B image selection, it is documented nowhere the vendor publishes, and it cannot be answered by reading anything - only by asking a board. READ ONLY: nothing on this path writes OCOTP in any form, and the burn would be irreversible and per board.

word.description: The whole 32-bit word as lower-case hex, because it is a bit field rather than a quantity and the fields this firmware does not decode are still in there: a later reader who learns what the upper byte means can recover it from an old capture.

read.description: False on a host build, where word is a sentinel that decodes to values no board can produce. A client must check this before concluding anything, and cannot be misled if it forgets.

sec_image_offset.description: Bits 23:16 - the secondary image base, in units of 256 KiB. Zero on a shipped part, and zero is exactly the finding that kills hardware A/B: the secondary image would live at the primary's address.

sec_image_size.description: Bits 15:12, the secondary image size field, decoded beside the offset so nobody has to shift by hand.

state.description: Audio path state as current_state() encodes it: 2 no carrier locked (or unclassified), 3 carrier with PCM classification, 4 carrier with DTS classification. An integer on the wire, matching UDP payload byte 2.

carrier.description: S/PDIF receiver PLL lock, 0|1 on the wire.

format.description: Classified input format code from UDP payload byte 23; an integer on the wire.

model_origin.description: Which stager produced the running DSP model: "default" the const factory model, "sd" the model loaded from /aius/dsp.json, "put" a model installed by PUT /api/dsp/config. It sits beside source because source is a two-word vocabulary that can only say whether an override is applied; a PUT-installed model reports source "sd" and model_origin "put". GET /api/dsp/config deliberately does NOT serve this key: its parser rejects any tenth top-level key, so emitting it there would break every GET-modify-PUT round trip.

dsp_config_pending.description: 1 while a staged DSP model is awaiting a block boundary, so source and model_origin above describe the staged model rather than the applied one. The dsp_ prefix is load-bearing here: config_valid / config_error describe the public aius.json config, not the DSP model.

dsp_staged_generation.description: The per-staging counter GET /api/dsp/config serves as staged_generation; it advances when a PUT's SD write commits (not at accept, so a faulted write leaves it unchanged) even on a carrier-less board, where nothing ever applies.

sd_filesystem.description: Volume type read by the SD probe while it held the mounted card. "none" is no card; "unknown" is a mounted volume whose type the driver does not name, exFAT included.

network_mode.description: "dhcp" when a DHCP lease is bound on the current network generation and the stack holds an address; "offline" in every other supervisor state. Static addressing was removed, so "static" is unreachable and retired. The same value is byte 1 of the UDP status payload, whose encoder accepts 0 and 1 only.

link.description: Ethernet link up, 0|1 on the wire (the NetDiag object carries the three-state raw values).

dhcp_pending.description: 1 while the adapter has started DHCP on the current network generation and no lease has been acquired yet. Read beside network_mode and ip: "offline" with dhcp_pending 1 is a lease in flight, "offline" with 0 is a generation that has not asked.

dhcp_discovers.description: Always 0: nothing in the pinned NativeEthernet stack counts DISCOVER frames without a vendor patch. The key is kept so it does not appear and disappear across builds; net_diag.current.tx_frames is the frame-level answer it cannot give.

dhcp_updates.description: DHCP leases the adapter's own lease callback has seen since init. It is never cleared, so it counts across network generations.

http_server_rebinds.description: Always 0. It counted an Ethernet server object dying and being re-begun mid-run, a state that does not exist after the network cutover: the listener is bound once per network generation. network_restarts is the nearest fact that is still real.

cpu_temp_c.description: Last accepted on-die temperature in degrees Celsius, sampled at most once a second. A reading outside -40..150 is rejected and leaves the previous value standing. 0 until the first accepted reading - check cpu_temp_valid before believing it.

cpu_temp_valid.description: 1 once a reading has been accepted. While 0, cpu_temp_c and cpu_temp_max_c are 0 because nothing has been measured, not because the die is at 0 C.

cpu_temp_max_c.description: Highest accepted reading since boot. Not cleared by POST /api/clear.

cpu_temp_age_ms.description: Milliseconds since the sample cpu_temp_c came from, so a stalled sampler is visible as an ageing reading rather than a plausible one. 0 while cpu_temp_valid is 0.

checkpoint_walltime_us.description: Lifetime per-checkpoint wall-time maxima in microseconds: element i is the longest interval ever observed from checkpoint i's ledger commit to the next checkpoint's, i.e. the worst case of the service that runs after checkpoint i. The stall detector the 2026-08-01 boot-lottery epoch-crawl investigation added; AIUS ID's cw=<id>:<us> carries only the worst pair on the bounded CDC budget, so a board whose HTTP has collapsed still names its stall.

checkpoint_cumulative_ms.description: Cumulative wall time per checkpoint in milliseconds, same slot meaning as checkpoint_walltime_us. Divided by loop_epoch this is the steady per-epoch cost of each service, which the maxima cannot attribute once boot-time spikes dominate them -- the boot-lottery defect's attribution tool.

audio_update_calls.description: Audio update ISR invocations since boot. Normal is the 93.75 Hz block rate against uptime; a value far above it convicts an ISR storm on this vector -- the boot-lottery defect's conviction counter.

audio_update_max_us.description: Longest single audio update ISR run in microseconds (normally sub-millisecond); a huge value convicts a stall inside the callback rather than a storm of invocations.

status_body_peak_bytes.description: Largest finished GET /api/status body this boot in bytes, the peak of the renders before this one (a body cannot state its own length). Compare against the 12,288-byte app body buffer; 0 on the first render.

http_shed.description: Phase 4f: requests answered 503 audio_busy (route sheds and SD job start sheds), the sum of http_shed_class. Reset by POST /api/clear.

http_dispatch_max_us.description: Phase 4f: every route's longest non-yielding stretch in one dispatch (us, nested producer passes excluded), unlisted routes included (F13). Reset by POST /api/clear.

sd_fifo_defers.description: Phase 4f: held decisions in FIFO mode while live input owned the ring with the margin short (F2, F9): each DEFER of an HTTP SD start and each hold of a root job at its start (no hold before the boot's first dsp.json load has ended; a started root job runs to its end). A count of holds, not of epochs: one epoch can add two. Reset by POST /api/clear.

http_shed_class.description: Phase 4f: 503 audio_busy answers per admission class, in order: full status, brief status, meters, events, settings PUT parse, directory listing, SD start (DMA), SD start (FIFO). Reset by POST /api/clear.

http_class_cost_us.description: Phase 4f: each admission class's current cost (us), in http_shed_class's order: the bucketed maximum of the longest stretch between yield points over the last 64 to 79 samples or about 8 to 10 s, whichever is shorter (a bucket closes after 16 samples or 2,000 ms; a shed adds no sample, so a shed class's cost still ages), or the declared seed until the first measurement and again once every bucket has aged out empty. Kept across POST /api/clear (F8).

status_render_failures.description: GET /api/status renders this boot that did not finish because the body outgrew the 12,288-byte app body buffer, each answered 500. Visible only in a later render that did finish; status_body_peak_bytes counts finished renders only.

network_state.description: Network supervisor state: 0 stack-start, 1 dhcp-wait, 2 online, 3 teardown, 4 backoff, 5 recovery-safe.

recovery_safe.description: 1 when the board booted into recovery-safe mode after two consecutive early watchdog resets. Recovery-safe mode services bounded USB only, so this field is observable here solely because the network happens to be up.

network_last_fault.description: Last network fault: 0 none, 1 dhcp-timeout, 2 link-lost, 3 stack-start, 4 dhcp-start, 5 listener, 6 udp, 7 socket, 8 teardown, 9 callback-overflow, 10 driver-protocol.

last_checkpoint.description: Runtime checkpoint persisted before the last service call: 0 reset-capture, 1 usb-rx, 2 usb-tx, 3 metrics, 4 network, 5 http, 6 udp, 7 replay, 8 sd, 9 audio, 10 epoch-complete. Only 10 marks a completed epoch. After a watchdog reset this names the service that stalled. The audio checkpoint was inserted at 9 by output-jitter Phase B and this vocabulary did not follow it until 2026-08-16; the encoder has always bounded the field against AIUS_BOOT_CHECKPOINT_EPOCH_COMPLETE, which is 10.

network_generation.description: Generation owning every current DHCP, listener, UDP and TCP resource. It advances on each network restart.

boot_generation.description: Retained boot counter, incremented once per boot.

reset_source.description: Raw retained reset-source register value captured at boot.

watchdog_early_resets.description: Consecutive watchdog resets that landed before epoch-complete. Two select recovery-safe mode; a new build revision or ten seconds of completed normal epochs clears the count.

network_restarts.description: Bounded network teardown/restart cycles since boot.

psram_mb.description: PSRAM the boot probe found on pad 1 (FlexSPI2 chip-select A1), in megabytes: 0 on a bare board, otherwise 8 or 16. The flight recorder's ring is sized from it, so 0 here is why GET /api/recorder reports state "absent".

psram_pad2_mb.description: Best-known PSRAM on the SECOND pad (FlexSPI2 chip-select A2, silkscreened FLASH), in megabytes. The core's boot probe never interrogates pad 2 while pad 1 is silent, so a lone chip soldered there is invisible to psram_mb; the firmware's own bounded probe answers 0, 8 or 16.

fault_record.description: The Teensy core's retained crash record (top 128 bytes of OCRAM, CRC'd, written by the core's fault handler and surviving every warm reset), previously readable only by printing CrashReport over USB. Deliberately never cleared, so it describes the most recent fault however many boots ago; null when no valid record stands (a clean history or a power cycle).

ota_dark.description: The retained dark-window forensic stamp (docs/plans/aius-ota-resilience.md Phase 1), decoded once at boot and sticky until the next entered activation window overwrites it; null when the retained slot carries no valid stamp (a fresh or power-cycled board). Served only on builds with AIUS_OTA, like ota_diag.

ab.description: The A/B slot state (docs/plans/aius-ota-resilience.md Phase 3): which slot this build runs from, the flash boot record's verdict and the chooser's retained trial ledger. null on the single-image build and on a slot build whose retained-ledger address contract failed.

AbState.description: A/B slot state: the running slot's identity, the ping-pong flash boot record (written only by the application) and the retained trial ledger (written only by the first-stage chooser). Slot values throughout: 0 none, 1 slot A, 2 slot B.

slot.description: The slot THIS build was linked for and runs from (the AIUS_AB_SLOT build identity).

record_valid.description: Whether a valid boot record was found; false is the fresh-migration state, and the record fields below read zero.

active_slot.description: The committed, known-good slot per the boot record.

pending_slot.description: The freshly-programmed slot on trial (0 when no trial is open). The running image commits it at the healthy mark; the chooser's budget bounds its boots.

sequence.description: The boot record's monotonic sequence; the higher valid ping-pong sector wins.

trial_budget.description: Boots the open trial may take before the chooser falls back (0 when no trial is open).

ledger_valid.description: Whether the retained trial ledger decoded at boot; false after a cold power cycle, which honestly restarts a trial count.

booted_slot.description: The ledger's own stamp of the slot the chooser booted, 0 when the ledger is invalid or the OLD per-slot chooser wrote it. The acceptance gate is ledger_valid && booted_slot != 0, so ledger_valid alone cannot say which chooser is live - and that difference decides whether a container must be signed with --slot. Distinct from slot, which falls back to the compile-time slot precisely when this is 0.

ledger_boots.description: Trial boots the chooser has launched for the ledger's record sequence.

ledger_fell_back.description: The chooser exhausted the trial budget and booted the active slot; the application persists the rollback and reports it below.

rollback_observed.description: THIS boot persisted a failed trial's rollback into the boot record (the fallback image cleaning up after the trial that never committed).

OtaDark.description: The dark-window forensic stamp: written to retained OCRAM by the activation sequencer (once on window entry, before every erase/program/readback step, and at the FAULTED or COMPLETED terminal), so a board that dies inside the flash window names its phase, step address, compare offset and fault code to the next boot that can speak -- surviving the WDOG reset the halt policy takes and a HalfKay reflash performed without a power cycle. The same headline rides the USB AIUS ID line as od=state:phase:fault:hex-address.

state.description: Stamp lifecycle, value-for-value AiusOtaDarkStampState: 1 entered (begin() passed, nothing erased -- or the first step wedged), 2 step (the operation at step_address was in flight when the board died), 3 faulted (the sequencer halted honestly; fault names why), 4 completed (the window finished and the reset was deliberate).

phase.description: The sequencer phase at the stamp, value-for-value AiusOtaActivatePhase: 1 erase-head, 2 body, 3 program-head, 4 ready-to-reset, 5 faulted.

fault.description: The typed AiusOtaActivateFault on a faulted stamp (0 none): which check or primitive said no.

rehearsal.description: True when the stamp was taken against the rehearsal's scratch window: the same sequence and stamping path, but the boot region was never touched -- never mistake a rehearsal's injected fault for a field brick.

primitive_fault.description: The refusing primitive's own return value (0 none), latched beside the typed fault.

step_address.description: Absolute flash address of the operation the stamp describes: the op about to run (state step), or the failing op (state faulted; 0 when the fault has no address, e.g. a withdrawn session).

compare_offset.description: Absolute image offset of the first byte the in-window readback compare found wrong, for a VERIFY fault; 4294967295 spells no compare fault.

programmed_bytes.description: Image bytes programmed when the stamp was taken.

verified_bytes.description: Image bytes read back and compared clean when the stamp was taken.

steps_taken.description: Sequencer steps completed when the stamp was taken.

steps_total.description: The exact fault-free step count for this image (aius_ota_activate_step_bound), the denominator for a progress fraction.

image_digest_prefix.description: First 8 bytes of the payload SHA-256 of the image the window was programming, as lowercase hex -- names WHICH image the stamp belongs to.

dark_window_cycles.description: Accumulated DWT cycles spent inside the dark window at the stamp (600 MHz on this part), unconverted so the retained record's numbers reach the reader untouched.

OtaDiag.description: Staged firmware-upgrade snapshot (docs/plans/aius-ota-upgrade.md), served only on the teensy41-optical build that sets the AIUS_OTA option; absent when OTA is compiled out. The same facts the dedicated GET /api/ota document carries, folded beside the other diagnostics so a status poller sees the upgrade without a second route.

state.description: Upgrade lifecycle, value-for-value AiusOtaState: 0 idle, 1 offered, 2 staging, 3 staged, 4 verified, 5 armed, 6 activation-requested, 7 failed. This slice stops at 5 (armed); activation is the later device-gated slice.

staged_bytes.description: Container bytes received so far (256-byte header plus staged payload), file-relative like the client's Content-Range; 0 before an image is offered.

total_bytes.description: Full container size (256-byte header plus the header's image_length payload); 0 before an image is offered.

fault.description: The AiusOtaStatus that drove a FAILED state (0 none), latched so a digest, signature or IVT-bounds refusal survives the request that caused it.

key_fingerprint.description: First 8 bytes of SHA-256(compiled-in public key) as lowercase hex, the swap point for a key rotation.

test_key.description: True only while the compiled-in key is the published-seed TEST fixture keypair, whose secret needs no repo access. False since the 2026-08-04 rotation to the repo-committed HOME key (firmware/config/ota-home-signing-key.*; the repository is the deployment's declared trust boundary, and production rotation to an off-repo key remains the documented later step). key_fingerprint says WHICH key either way.

activation_available.description: The runtime activation latch: false at every boot, and true only after the operator has flipped it (POST /api/ota/enable-activation) following the on-bench scratch-sector recovery proof. While it is false the activate route answers 409 and this flag is how a page knows not to offer the step.

self_test_flash.description: The item-5 scratch-sector recovery proof's verdict: never-run until the operator triggers POST /api/ota/self-test-flash, then pass if the real erase/program/read-back matched (the driver's LUT use did not break XIP) or fail otherwise.

psram.description: Whether PSRAM is fitted anywhere the composition can stage into (pad 1 via the core, or pad 2 via the firmware's bounded probe). Activation and the rehearsal stage the image into PSRAM and are refused (ota_no_psram) without it.

activation_fault.description: The last activation or rehearsal refusal reason, so a status poller sees why a deferred flash act did not run: no PSRAM fitted, the SD-to-PSRAM copy failed, the pre-window verification refused, or the flash geometry refused (rehearsal: the image reaches the scratch window).

rehearsal.description: The 2026-08-01 re-proof's verdict: never-run until the operator triggers POST /api/ota/rehearse (or /api/ota/rehearse-fault), then pass if the run reached its arm's expected terminal -- the emulated reset for the positive arm, the head-compare FAULTED halt for the fault-injected one.

rehearsal_fault.description: The sequencer's AiusOtaActivateFault at the rehearsal's terminal (0 none): which check or primitive said no, when the verdict is fail -- and the expected VERIFY value on a passing fault-injected arm.

rehearsal_fault_injected.description: Which arm the verdict describes: true when the last rehearsal ran with the injected head-readback fault (the negative arm).

rehearsal_dark_us.description: The rehearsal's accumulated dark-window time in microseconds -- the operator-expectation number the plan's stall measurement deferred to bring-up evidence.

rehearsal_max_step_us.description: The longest single sequencer step (one erase, or one program+readback+compare) in microseconds, bounding the watchdog-feed cadence the dark window sustains.

OtaStatus.description: GET /api/ota body, assembled by the dispatcher (aius_optical_app.cpp) from the OTA status the composition root fills. Served by the teensy41-optical build; a build without OTA answers 404 ota_absent instead.

armed.description: The FEATURE LATCH ('may this device do OTA at all'), not the armed STATE. A reboot always comes up disarmed; the firmware arms it at composition on the OTA build.

state.description: Upgrade lifecycle. This slice stops at 'armed'.

next_offset.description: The FILE offset the next chunk must carry, so a resuming client reads it here instead of replaying a chunk.

image.description: The offered container's identity, from its parsed header; empty/zero before an offer. A field carrying a byte outside printable ASCII is published empty rather than escaped.

fingerprint.description: First 8 bytes of SHA-256(compiled-in public key) as lowercase hex.

test_key.description: True only while the compiled-in key is the published-seed TEST fixture keypair; false since the 2026-08-04 rotation to the repo-committed home key. The page banners TEST KEY on true.

activation_available.description: The runtime activation latch: false at every boot, true only after POST /api/ota/enable-activation. While false, POST /api/ota/activate answers 409 ota_activation_disabled.

fault.description: Wire token of the latched fault ('none' when clear), the same vocabulary a refusal answers with: ota_digest, ota_signature or ota_ivt after a failed verify.

verifier_fault.description: The injected Ed25519 verifier's own return value on a signature refusal (a live diagnostic, not persisted).

OtaChunkAck.description: PUT /api/ota/image answer. On success {"ok":true,"next_offset":N}; on an out-of-order chunk {"ok":false,"error":"ota_range","next_offset":N} so the client resumes from N (a FILE offset).

TxGate.description: The optical transmit gate's latched per-epoch decision and inputs, evaluated once per epoch at the replay checkpoint and never re-derived at request time (so this JSON and the physical pad cannot disagree within one poll). Policy: open iff carrier_locked or replay_running. On the bench build the actuator is pad 14's mux (dark = GPIO driven low, the same electrical state the carrier board's TX_ENABLE gate produces); an unavoidable ~ms silence-carrier blip exists at static construction ~300 ms after every reset, before setup()'s dark-set -- closed from setup() onward. In recovery-safe mode the gate stays frozen dark.

open.description: 1 while the pad routes SPDIF_OUT; 0 while the output is held dark.

carrier_locked.description: The latched S/PDIF receiver PLL lock at the last evaluation.

replay_running.description: The latched replay term: source is SWITCHING_TO_REPLAY (prebuffering counts, giving the sink lock lead time) or REPLAY. An EOF'd replay keeps this 1 until stopped or displaced by a carrier -- the accepted policy residue.

NetDiag.description: Network measurement surface. Diagnostic only: nothing here is a supervisor input, and it exists to replace inference about why the first DHCP attempt of a boot receives nothing. The six live values are read once per request; the two generation records are filled by calls the adapter makes once per network generation, never per epoch and never on the audio path.

link.description: NativeEthernet's cached link member (0 unknown, 1 up, 2 down). It is a variable, not a reading: its initial value is sampled inside beginNoWait() and thereafter only the FNET link service's callback updates it. This is the same value the boolean "link" field above renders.

link_live.description: A fresh link observation taken by asking the interface rather than the cache, same encoding as "link". The two disagreeing is the observation that convicts the cached member. FNET throttles the underlying PHY register read to one per 200 ms across all callers, and its own link service already polls at that rate, so this costs no additional MDIO traffic in practice.

dhcp_state.description: FNET's own DHCP client state from fnet_dhcp_cln_get_state(): 0 disabled, 1 init, 2 selecting (DISCOVER sent, waiting for OFFER), 3 requesting, 4 probing, 5 bound, 6 renewing, 7 rebinding, 8 init-reboot, 9 rebooting; 255 means no DHCP client is registered on the interface. The values come from a private enum in the pinned library's service/dhcp/fnet_dhcp_cln.c and are documented here rather than duplicated in firmware.

frames_valid.description: False when the driver refused the statistics call, in which case neither frame counter means anything.

dhcp_schedule_valid.description: True when the three schedule values below were read from the live FNET DHCP client. False (with zeros) when the stack is down or no client is registered. Added for the reopened periodic-WDOG second death mode: the death schedule must be read from the client's own option values, because reconstructing it from observed cadence proved unreliable (open-work register).

dhcp_lease_s.description: The bound lease's lease-time option in seconds, host byte order, as the FNET client holds it.

dhcp_t1_s.description: The renewal (T1) option in seconds - the timer whose expiry anchored the first (fixed) death mode at ~boot+1,905 s.

dhcp_t2_s.description: The rebinding (T2) option in seconds - a candidate anchor for the surviving ~6,176 s death mode, decidable once these served values replace the cadence reconstruction.

fnet_heap_valid.description: True when the two netheap readings below came from the live FNET stack; false (with zeros) before fnet_init or with the stack down.

fnet_heap_free_b.description: FNET netheap free bytes at the read (fnet_free_mem_status). The conviction instrument for the count-anchored death hypothesis: a per-connection leak shows as this value falling linearly with http_requests, and its floor names the exhaustion the HTTP job wedges on.

fnet_heap_largest_b.description: Largest single allocation the netheap could satisfy at the read (fnet_malloc_max) - fragmentation shows as this falling faster than free bytes.

tx_frames.description: Ethernet frames the MAC has transmitted since its counters were cleared, from the FEC's RMON_T_PACKETS hardware counter. The counters are zeroed by fnet_netif_init(), which only the generation that initialises the interface performs.

rx_frames.description: Ethernet frames the MAC has received, from RMON_R_PACKETS.

first.description: The first network generation that ever ended, retained rather than overwritten because that is the generation under investigation and nothing can read this surface until a later one has brought HTTP up. Null until a generation has ended.

current.description: The live generation's record, still accumulating until it ends.

NetDiagGeneration.description: One network generation's measurements. Every *_ms value is an offset from that generation's stack start, in milliseconds; a measurement that did not happen is null rather than 0, so "did not happen" cannot be read as "happened immediately".

stack_started_ms.description: Board uptime in milliseconds when this generation's stack start began. It is the record's ONE absolute value and the anchor every other *_ms offset is measured from: without it the phases of a generation can be timed against each other but not placed in the boot, which is what separates "the stack came up slowly" from "the stack started late".

netif_init.description: Whether this generation's beginNoWait() performed the real fnet_netif_init() (1) or found the interface already initialised and skipped it (2); 0 means the probe was unavailable. Within one boot the first generation performs it and later ones skip it, which is why the two are not running the same code.

stack_start_blocking_ms.description: How long beginNoWait() itself took. It is not "no wait" on the generation that initialises the interface: that path resets the PHY and blocks in FNET's autonegotiation wait for up to 2000 ms. Saturates at 65535.

link_at_stack_start.description: The cached link value the stack-start gate read immediately after beginNoWait() returned, same encoding as NetDiag.link. Unknown (0) when the stack failed to start and the read was never reached.

link_up_source.description: Which observer released this generation's STACK_STARTED: 0 none, 1 the stack-start read of the cached member, 2 the FNET link service's callback, 3 a later poll read of the cached member. 1 means the gate was released by an init-time snapshot rather than by an observation.

link_up_ms.description: When that release happened. Null when link-up was never reported.

link_callbacks.description: Link callbacks of either polarity the generation saw, from the FNET link service's own polling.

link_callback_up_ms.description: When the link service's callback first delivered connected -- the answer to "when did a fresh read first report up", independent of which observer released the gate. The service starts each generation with its connection flag clear, so an already-up link still produces one callback. Null when it never did.

rx_ready_source.description: What released this generation's receive-readiness gate, and therefore its STACK_STARTED: 0 none (the gate is still closed, or link-up was never reached), 1 not required (the generation skipped fnet_netif_init() and never waited), 2 counter (the MAC clocked a frame in, so DHCP started on evidence), 3 deadline (nothing arrived inside the bound and DHCP started anyway). Without it the gap between link-up and dhcp_start_ms is unattributed.

rx_ready_ms.description: When that release happened. Null unless rx_ready_source is 2 or 3, the only two values that name a moment.

dhcp_start_ms.description: When START_DHCP ran. Null when the generation never reached it.

dhcp_state_at_start.description: FNET's DHCP client state immediately after dhcpStart() returned, same encoding as NetDiag.dhcp_state.

end_reason.description: How the generation ended: 0 still live, 1 teardown, 2 online. First end wins, so a generation that bound a lease and was retired later keeps the moment it succeeded.

end_ms.description: When it ended. Null while it is still live.

dhcp_state_at_end.description: FNET's DHCP client state at that moment -- the discriminating value when a DHCP deadline expires. 2 (selecting) says the client believes it sent a DISCOVER and is waiting for an OFFER.

link_at_end.description: The last cached link value the adapter had read when the generation ended, same encoding as NetDiag.link.

link_live_at_end.description: A fresh link read taken at the end itself, for comparison with link_at_end at the decisive moment.

frames_valid.description: False when the MAC's counters were unavailable at either end of the DHCP window.

tx_frames.description: Frames the MAC transmitted between START_DHCP and the end of the generation. This is the frame-level discriminator: 0 across a DHCP window that timed out means no DISCOVER was ever handed to the MAC, while a non-zero count means the MAC clocked one out and it was lost past the FEC. Null when frames_valid is false.

rx_frames.description: Frames the MAC received over the same window. Null when frames_valid is false.

Events.description: One page of the device event ring (32 entries deep since aius-input-recovery Phase 1; the page stays 8). The page holds the oldest retained entries after `cursor`, so a poller that fell behind the ring resumes at the oldest survivor rather than losing the page too; event_overflows on GET /api/status counts what was overwritten before it could be read.

cursor.description: The cursor the request carried (0 when absent).

next.description: The cursor to pass for the following page: the last sequence served when this page is full (8 entries), else the newest sequence the ring holds. A full page means more is pending; poll again at once.

Event.description: One ring entry. Types 1-3 are transitions; 4-10 are counter edges, emitted from the epoch loop at most once per counter per epoch, so a burst is one event carrying the delta rather than one event per increment; 11-13 are clock episodes; 14-18 are the output-glitch family, posted from the audio producer at the instant the thing happened because each names a bounded event with a size.

type.description: Allocated once, never renumbered or reused; a reader must ignore a value it does not know. 1 state (S/PDIF lock or pipeline classification moved), 2 test tone toggled, 3 replay stopped by itself, 4 audio overruns, 5 datagrams that failed decode, 6 UDP service calls over budget, 7 config parse failed, 8 network stack restarted, 9 DHCP lease bound, 10 retained watchdog early-reset count, 11 accepted live nominal rate, 12 refused-rate episode, 13 failed clock apply, 14 gate-open underrun episode (posted when it ends), 15 latency-governor trim, 16 accepted same-nominal PLL trim, 17 missed transmit fills, 18 a compressed access unit refused by its own syncframe CRC and replaced by silence.

detail.description: Type-specific. 2: 1 running / 0 stopped. 3: the replay stop reason. 4, 5, 6, 9, 10: the counter's advance since the previous epoch, clamped to 65535. 7: the AiusConfigErrorCode. 8: the AiusNetFault that caused the restart. 11: the accepted rate in Hz. 12: the measured rate in Hz, or 0 for an unsupported decoded block. 13: the AiusClockApplyResult. 14: the episode's substituted frames, saturated to 65535 (its start and duration are in clock.underrun_episodes). 15: the frames that trim dropped. 16: |target - nominal| in millihertz, saturated; the sign is clock.trim_ppm on the next status read. 17: missed fills since the previous post. 18: the rejected frame's byte length (64-3840 for AC-3), which is what names the unit against a capture.
